The improved RCA relies on QFD for the standardized and comprehensive fault-mode analysis and utilizes inverse QFD to achieve logical reasoning. With DEMATEL, it recognizes the relevance of fault modes and sequence fault modes in terms of importance based on their frequency of occurrence. Corrective actions were developed according to quality requirements to improve their effectiveness and correctness. The improved RCA was proved to be correct and operable as revealed in the case analysis and conclusion.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Single Event Effect-hardened Design for SRAM-FPGA-Based System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) static random-access memory (SRAM) based Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) technology has been widely used within the space industry due to its cost-effectiveness and high-performance attributes. However, its original design primarily caters to benign operating environments. The deleterious impact of space radiation, particularly the single-event effect (SEE), poses a significant threat to the operational reliability of SRAM-FPGA devices in space applications. In order to fortify these devices against the challenges of the space radiation environment and ensure the utmost system reliability, this paper initiates by providing an overview of the SEE-related issues pertaining to SRAM-FPGA and offers insights into general hardening design solutions. Subsequently, this paper introduces a comprehensive multilevel SEE hardening design strategy, encompassing component selection, as well as hardware and software hardening methods at the board-level. Furthermore, it delves into system-level design protective measures. A real-world case study is presented to exemplify the practical implementation of these hardening techniques that enhance system reliability.

articleTitle: Life Assessment of Grounding Material Incorporating Corrosion Environmental Factors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Environmental factors play a crucial role in the reliability and performance of structures and systems. This study evaluates the influence of environmental factors such as oxygen content, pH, and salt concentration on corrosion, which affect the reliability of grounding systems. Based on this, we propose and validate a novel corrosion model and correlate it with the life characteristics of grounding systems. Sensitivity analysis and confidence interval estimation were employed for the evaluation of the model. The results provide insights into the grounding system's reliability, which is essential for safe and effective system operation.

articleTitle: Reliability Design and Application of Large Complex Spacecraft Network System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: With the development of wireless communication technology and Ethernet, several spacecraft have established an integrated space-ground network, using network technology to transmit high-rate data. Especially in large complex spacecraft, their network systems often undertake the transmission of a large amount of data related to spacecraft flight control, state monitoring, on-orbit experiment support, and other functions. Since network reliability directly affects the safety of spacecraft, its study has attracted significant attention. Aiming at high-reliability requirements of spacecraft information systems based on the conventional topology design of spacecraft network systems, the design method of ensuring network connectivity is presented from the aspects of the device, single-module network system, and multi-module network system designs. The method not only meets the spacecraft mission requirements but also improves the reliability of the network system.

articleTitle: Quantitative Safety Analysis Method for Complex Equipment System Based on FRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As complex equipment systems evolve to higher levels of sophistication, conventional risk and safety assessment techniques may find it challenging to offer a comprehensive risk analysis, especially in discerning the interactions and linkages among diverse functional elements. The functional resonance analysis method (FRAM) provides a functional viewpoint for system understanding and the analysis of potential hazards emerging from these functional couplings. This study devised a quantitative approach to assess the safety level of intricate equipment systems, with a focus on functional couplings as framed by FRAM. Quantitative scrutiny was applied to the interrelationships among functions within the system, culminating in an evaluation of the system's overall safety level. The viability of the proposed methodology was corroborated through a case study.

articleTitle: A Scenario-Goal Hybrid Method for Reliability Requirement Capture
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In this paper, a scenario-goal hybrid reliability requirement capture method is proposed. This method combines scenario description and goal determination by utilizing the concept of requirement chunks. Specifically, it introduces the concept of a reliability requirement chunk (RRC), which is tailored to the nonfunctional characteristics of aircraft reliability. The RRC defines the types and features of aircraft reliability requirements and achieves the reliability requirements through composition strategy, alternative strategy, and refinement strategy during requirement capture. The scenario-goal hybrid reliability requirement capture method obtains the reliability requirements of the aircraft scientifically, reasonably, and completely in all operational scenarios. Additionally, it facilitates the reasonable provision of requirements propagation, reliability requirements, and design objectives during the aircraft conceptualization and design phases. The paper outlines the specific steps of the reliability requirement capture process and demonstrates the engineering applicability of this method by acquiring reliability requirements for civil aircraft in a typical flight profile.

articleTitle: MEMS Sensitive Structure Sand and Dust Pollution Test and Its Degradation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The sensitive structures of certain devices containing micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) must be directly exposed to the working environment, making them vulnerable to contamination by dust and other pollutants in that environment. Consequently, this contamination degrades the performance of the device, impacting both its working life and stability. Existing test methods, such as GB/T 4208–2017 and GB/T 2423.37-2006, are not entirely suitable for evaluating the sand and dust contamination test of these MEMS devices. To address these issues, a thermistor-based test structure was designed and processed to develop an evaluation method suitable for testing the sand and dust contamination sensitive MEMS structures. The test results indicate that, unlike other hermetically sealed electronic devices, the imposition of electrical stress and cycling of the operating voltage “on-off” during the test does not increase dust accumulation. Furthermore, due to sand and dust contamination, the thermistor value of the device drifts during operation. This drift primarily arises from increased thermal resistance between the heating element of the device and the surrounding environment, resulting from the accumulation of sand and dust, which results in the increase of temperature of the heating element and ultimately results in an elevated thermistor value. This study can provide support for the structural design and package design of MEMS sensitive structures, and provide a basis for the identification and inspection of related products and the development of detailed specifications.

articleTitle: Sensitive Stress Analysis via Reliability Enhancement Test for Mechanical Aerospace Products
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: With advancements in aerospace technology, the development goal of future mechanical aerospace products is to create low-cost, high-reliability, and generalized products to satisfy the requirements of different mission profiles. However, traditional development tests for mechanical products are typically not implemented under environmental conditions or operational stress beyond the design limit. Hence, they cannot obtain the design and working limits of the product. Consequently, providing quantitative support for the adaptability of the developed product is difficult. With the increased development needs of mechanical aerospace products, sensitive stresses affecting product quality have been identified in this paper by analyzing historical quality problems of similar products and promoting FMEA analysis. The analysis of sensitive stress via a reliability enhancement test for mechanical aerospace products has been proposed to fully stimulate weakness of mechanics and improve the inherent reliability of products through design improvements.

articleTitle: Research on Elastic Wave Numerical Simulation Method of Thermal Protection Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Thermal Protection Structures (TPS) are critical structures for reusable space vehicles, which safety and reliability are of vital importance. This paper investigates structural health monitoring method based on the elastic wave of piezoelectric sensor for TPS of reusable spacecraft, proposes a numerical simulation method of TPS elastic wave based on finite element, focusing on the simulation problem of elastic wave propagation force-electricity-thermal multi-physics field coupling of thermal protection structures under the influence of temperature gradient, taking titanium alloy TPS as a case study. Based on the elastic wave signals and propagating wave fields under the influence of temperature gradient obtained from the simulation, the effect of temperature gradient on elastic wave propagation characteristics is analyzed to provide a basis for the subsequent health monitoring of thermal protection structures.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in a 10 kV Transmission Line Using a One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network Embedded with a Mish Activation Function
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Efficient and accurate identification and diagnosis of faults are essential for the effective operation of power systems. The existing data-driven fault diagnosis methods typically encounter challenges associated with high computational load and low model training speeds. To address these problems, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) integrated with the Mish activation function. This approach enables automatic feature learning from signal datasets, thereby facilitating fault detection and diagnosis. To evaluate the proposed method, a 10 kV small current neutral point ungrounded system is established using Simulink simulation software. Fault signals are acquired through fault injection, and fault classification is realized using the proposed fault diagnosis framework. In addition, the generalizability of the proposed method is enhanced by introducing noise and measurement errors into the diagnostic data. Experimental results show that the proposed method can accurately detect and classify faults with high robustness and generalizability and is thus suitable for online protection of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Model-Based Safety Analysis for Aero-Engine Digital Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The model-based safety analysis (MBSA) method is used to analyze the safety of a digital control system given the difficulty in using the traditional safety analysis method for aero-engine digital control system. Based on the traditional safety analysis method and combined with the characteristics of MBSA, this paper studies the application flow of MBSA in the safety analysis of digital control system and the modeling method of the safety model. This paper focuses on the application phase of MBSA and the model building method suitable for digital control system. A safety model is introduced into the preliminary system safety assessment to help conduct the analysis. The modeling is completed using the failure logic modeling approach and modeling process based on the characteristics of aero-engine digital control system by comparing the two modeling approaches of extended system model and failure logic modeling.

articleTitle: Reliability Estimation Based on Weibull Distributions
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Distributions modeling and reliability analysis are crucial to Micro Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS) devices for their operation environment is complex and require high reliability. This paper illustrates the reliability research of a MEMS flowmeter with lifetime distribution model. The temperature stress <tex>$(T_{s})$</tex> is used to finish accelerated aging test. After accelerated aging test with both the current degradation status and historical degradation trajectory, the degradation results are achieved. Then the minimum drift was 82.01% after accelerated aging test. The characteristics of these MEMS flowmeter units in different accelerated aging process are analyzed. Finally, it proved that Weibull Distribution (WD) is the better mode for the MEMS flowmeter acceleration lifetime with mixed mixture method and Standard residual error method of Goodness-of-fit tests. This research will benefit for modern complex systems reliability analysis of MEMS flowmeter units.

articleTitle: Study on Evaluation and Validation Methods of Digital Model based on VV&A
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: For development of the Digital Economy according to the 14th Five-Year Plan and to address the need for evaluating and validating digital models, this discussion focuses on the key challenges associated with such evaluations and validations. These challenges stem from the inherent complexity and diversity of digital models, the presence of heterogeneous and diverse model data, and the scarcity of real-world measurement data. Furthermore, we propose an approach to digital model evaluation and validation based on Verification, Validation, and Accreditation (VV&A). This approach involves classifying digital models according to their intended applications, representation methods, and storage format. By conducting targeted validation and evaluation processes to specific model types, this method addresses the primary challenges encountered in digital model evaluation and validation.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Key Parameters in an Accelerated Degradation Test Scheme for Rubber Sealing Rings
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In order to determine the lifespan of rubber sealing rings, an accelerated performance degradation test is commonly employed. The key parameters for this test are the number of test profiles and the quantity of measurement points within each profile. In this paper, a numerical simulation method is proposed for calculating the parameters. It incorporates considerations of test errors, including intercept error, slope error and the average distance error between two lines to gauge the precision and quality of the tests. The objective is to investigate how different quantities of test profiles and measurement points impact test errors, enabling the identification of a test configuration with minimal error. It is determined that test errors can be kept within 4 % when each test profile contains 11 or more measurement points and within 25% when there are four or more test profiles.

articleTitle: Factorial Design Approach for Importance Analysis of System Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The importance of system component parameters signifies their effect on system reliability. Most existing methods for importance analysis are computationally intensive, i.e., they require a large number of observations, or do not consider the features of complex dynamic systems. This study proposes a method to calculate the importance measure of component parameters on the basis of factors in factorial design. Two examples are presented, one for the structural importance of fault trees and the other for the importance of the component failure rate of a phased mission system (PMS). The proposed measure can take conventional structural importance as a special case and accurately reflect the characteristics of the PMS.

articleTitle: Product Testability Testing and Evaluation Implementation Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The process of testability tests for infrared detectors is designed to elucidate the requirements for testability test verification and propose the implementation guidelines. This is in line with the actual demands of testability verification for product test technology. The paper also clarifies the evaluation methods for three key quantitative indicators: fault detection rate, fault isolation rate, and false alarm rate. These efforts have yielded positive results in actual test verification, offering valuable insights for product testability test verification.

articleTitle: Design and Application of a Model-Based Intelligent Production System for Aerospace Servo Products
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This study introduces the pioneering “system flow model” to the production site of aerospace servo products. We applied a “five-dimensional integration” intelligent production system based on digital twin technology [1] and quality management theory. Through this, we achieved holistic planning, management, diagnosis, and re-optimization of production activities. The methodology addressed prevalent issues, including inadequate system management and control capabilities at production sites, underutilization of data, limited production information sharing, and over-reliance on personnel expertise. During implementation, we employed innovative system quality management tools and methods, such as value stream mapping, system diagrams, the PDPC method, multi-PDCA loops, and IE measurement tools. These tools were instrumental in identifying and diagnosing production process bottlenecks, optimizing production processes, and enabling real-time monitoring of production processes and product quality. The established intelligent production management system marks a significant stride for enterprises aiming to advance their intelligent manufacturing strategies and achieve industrial upgrades. Compared with traditional production modes, our approach has increased production capacity more than threefold. It yielded commendable outcomes in safety, quality, efficiency, cost, and personnel, chiefly exemplified by the lean production mode, end-to-end transparent quality management, methodical site layout, continual personnel enhancement, and system flexibility. Furthermore, the study's approach to designing and implementing an intelligent production system rooted in the system flow model offers other organizations a comprehensive and scientific blueprint for digital transformation, paving the way for swift and sustainable industry growth.

articleTitle: Reflection of the Six Properties Collaborative Work Based on MBSE
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Under the requirements of high reliability and safety, the new generation of manned launch vehicles has inherited practical results obtained from the “Six Properties” collaborative work combined with the experience of traditional “Six Properties.” We use model-based systems engineering (MBSE) ideas, methods, tools, and measures; propose a model-based failure-oriented “Six Properties” collaborative development process and method; and establish a digital model of “Six Properties.” This model integrates the traditional “Six Properties” work and collaborative processes and implements advanced development concepts such as comprehensive, collaborative, and iterative ideas for successfully integrating MBSE into the “Six Properties” work. The entire life cycle and system utilize the parallel implementation and iteration of the “Six Properties” design and functional performance design. Our model promotes the development of the “Six Properties” system engineering theory and practice in the aerospace field.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Growth Methods for Ship Power and Electromechanical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Reliability growth is an important method for improving product reliability, and it has been studied extensively in theory and applied in the fields of aerospace and aviation in engineering. The application of reliability growth technology in the shipbuilding industry started relatively late and is focused on the electronic equipment. This article is based on reliability growth, and it systematically studies the reliability growth model, analysis of weaknesses in reliability, and improvement methods of ship power and electromechanical equipment to provide a method for reliability growth.

articleTitle: Maintenance Strategy of the Airborne System Based on the Markov Decision Process
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The reliability of the airborne system has a significant impact on the safety of the aircraft. Reasonable maintenance of the airborne system can save maintenance costs as well as ensure the safety and reliability of the system. A maintenance model for the airborne dynamic system is developed based on Markov decision process. The model defines the state of the system, selects the end of the flight as the decision epoch, and obtains the state transition probability considering the natural deterioration and maintenance process. The goal of the model is to minimize the total expected discount cost of long-term operation. In addition, the maintenance cost also considers the risk factors. This model uses the value iteration method to get the optimal decision by backtracking step by step. Finally, an application example is given by taking an aircraft AC power supply system as an example.

articleTitle: Application of Non-Parametric Estimation Method in Reliability Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The reliability of satellites determines the service capability of the system. In this paper, a non-parametric estimation method is used to analyze the in-orbit reliability of satellites. Through case analysis, non-parametric estimation can accurately estimate the average reliability level of satellites, which has a good reference value for the reliability estimation of navigation satellites designed with the same platform. Additionally, Weibull configuration parameters obtained from satellite in-orbit operation data can continuously modify the reliability curve obtained from ground tests, thus providing a basis for formulating more scientific test schemes.

articleTitle: Research on Full-Cycle Management of Equipment Reliability Improvement in Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper briefly describes the full-cycle management of nuclear power plant engineering design, civil construction, commissioning, operation, and maintenance. It introduces the common problems of equipment quality defects and analyzes the equipment management requirements and regulations of nuclear power plants in various stages of its life-cycle. Based on typical system equipment defect cases, this paper discusses the key points of reliability improvement in each stage of equipment management and puts forward several suggestions. The suggestions for corrective action include paying attention to equipment design and selection, improving equipment quality supervision and inspection, improving preventive maintenance strategy, and strengthening equipment status performance monitoring. The goal of information sharing, closed-loop control, process tracking, and continuous optimization of equipment reliability management is realized with the help of the full-cycle management process. The results of this study contribute toward promoting the standardization, normalization, and improvement in the level of equipment reliability management in nuclear power plants.

articleTitle: System Resilience Assessment Based on FRAM and DBN
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In a social technology system, intricate interactions and coupling relationships exist among the various components. Traditional approaches struggle to effectively assess the effects of risk factors on the overall performance effectively of the system. To address the challenge of complex system resilience assessment, a method integrating the functional resonance analysis method (FRAM) and dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) is introduced. Initially, a functional interaction model for the mission process of the system is constructed based on FRAM, and underlying risk factors are identified. Subsequently, a DBN model is established, predicated based on the interconnections among risk factors, resilience attribute nodes, and the functional state of the system. Furthermore, the resilience of the system is quantified, and pivotal factors influencing it are ascertained through sensitivity analysis. As a case study, the carrier-based aircraft take-off and landing system is evaluated to proffer recommendations for ensuring the regular operation of the system.

articleTitle: Requirement Analysis Technology for Maintainability Design of Aircraft Based on Maintenance Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Currently, the model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach is extensively employed in the development of new aircraft. Persisting with experience-based methodologies for maintenance design would invariably result in a disconnect between an aircraft's functional performance and its maintainability. This article delves into contemporary trends in aircraft maintainability technology and investigates the technology for capturing maintainability design requirements based on maintenance scenarios. Utilizing the MBSE framework, the study addresses the classification of maintenance design requirements, the modeling of distinct maintenance scenarios, and the determination of specific maintenance design requirements. A method for maintainability requirement analysis is developed, aiming to amalgamate the maintenance requirement management process with the aircraft design process. Through this research, we strive to advance a requirements-driven approach to aircraft maintainability. This approach facilitates synchronous feedback, coordinated actions, and integrated design, thereby influencing design decisions to optimize maintainability.

articleTitle: Influence of Paraffin Shielding on the Fast Neutron Environmental Adaptability of a Complementary Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The traditional power supply scheme of solar panels and batteries cannot satisfy the energy demand of deep space exploration, high-power payloads, and other missions as the space industry develops. Therefore, space nuclear reactors are inevitable choices. In contrast to the traditional power supply scheme, space reactors produce a large number of neutrons and gamma rays during the mission period. These neutral particles possess much higher penetration ability than electrons, protons, and other charged particles, resulting in insufficient shielding ability of traditional radiation protection methods. Thus, the shielding characteristics of materials must be studied to evaluate the fast neutron environmental adaptability of devices. However, no method for assessing neutron damage has reached maturity. This study adopted the displacement damage factor theory and considered the dark current and fixed pattern noise of a complementary Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor image sensor as sensitive parameters. The shielding efficiency of paraffin for fast neutrons through paraffin shielding and an unshielded control group were examined and subsequently verified through simulations. The test results showed that 4 cm paraffin could shield approximately 30% of 2.5 MeV fast neutrons, which has certain application value.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Capacitive Pressure Transmitters Considering Natural Degradation and Random Shocks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Capacitive pressure transmitters are subject to natural degradation, such as aging and wear, as well as random shocks induced by the external environment. The measurement accuracy change of capacitive pressure transmitters is a failure problem caused by natural degradation and random shocks. A DIC(Digital Image Correlation) experiment and finite element simulation are used to analyze the displacement results of capacitive pressure transmitters under different pressure variations. Thus, a reliability assessment model for capacitive pressure transmitters characterized by pressure-displacement and considering the effects of external shocks is established. The reliability modeling reveals that the measurement accuracy is more susceptible to failures caused by random shocks, and the proposed method can be used for condition monitoring and reliability assessment of capacitive pressure transmitters.

articleTitle: Safety Risk Assessment Method for Accidental Explosion of Aircraft in Flight
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Analysis of safety-critical items is important for equipment development. Under the large systematic combat mode, missile equipment faces numerous system-level risks including security threats to aircraft, ships, and other equipment and facilities under specific conditions. Therefore, an urgent requirement to strengthen the ability of specific risk analysis and quantitative assessment of missile flight exists. Considering the specific risk of accidental explosion that can occur during missile flight and the safety of missile flight tests, this study focuses on the safety risk of explosion events to launch platforms and other missiles using theoretical analysis methods to model and analyze the trajectory of fragments produced by missile explosions. The impact of fragments after the explosion of energetic products such as missile engines is quantified. This study provides support for the optimal design of flight test schemes.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of the Effect of a Floating Junction Terminal Structure on the Dual-Zone JTE Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Silicon-carbide floating junction devices have garnered significant attention owing to their potential to surpass the unipolar limit. While there have been experimental results on silicon-carbide floating junction devices, there is limited research on the terminals of these devices, and further exploration of the design principles for floating junction devices is required. In this study, we propose two floating junction terminal structures: continuous and discontinuous. We investigate the performance differences between these two structures using a two-zone junction-termination-extension (JTE) surface terminal structure for the floating junction device. Simulation results demonstrate that the floating junction device with a continuous terminal structure exhibits superior electrical characteristics. Compared to the non-continuous terminal structure, the continuous terminal structure reduces the surface terminal length by 35.7%, extends the ion implantation dose window by 135%, and increases the interface charge tolerance by 33%. We believe that the findings presented in this paper will effectively guide the internal terminal design of floating junction devices, enhance the reliability of such devices, and facilitate their wider application in power electronics.

articleTitle: Optimization of “One-Station” Aircraft Carrier Ground Crew Allocation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To improve the efficiency of the carrier support system, this paper focuses on the problem of allocation of ground support personnel in the support process. Considering “one-station” support as an example, in this study, we utilized the AnyLogic simulation software to conduct discrete event modeling for the support process, adopted minimum average support time as the objective function, set relevant constraints, and used the OptQuest tool to re-assign the support tasks to other support team personnel. The results show that this optimization method can reduce the support time and improve the combat efficiency. The established optimization model of support resource allocation is helpful for decision makers to train and cultivate support personnel and has certain reference significance for the improvement of aircraft carrier recovery support efficiency.

articleTitle: Reliability Design and Implementation of China Space Station EVA
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To achieve the requirements of long-term safety and reliable operation, the capability for maintenance and assembly to support the space station through extravehicular activity (EVA) is essential. Owing to the unique characteristic of the spacecraft's extravehicular space environment, EVA is a highly complex and hazardous space mission. On the basis of analyzing the mission objectives of outbound activities, the safety design method for EVA and implementation of in-orbit operations of China “Tiangong” as well as the future application of the safety design method for EVA in manned lunar and planetray explorations is prospected.

articleTitle: Integrated Design Process of General Quality Characteristics of Clustered UAS by MBSE
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As the mission modes and application scenarios of clustered unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) continue to diversify, the inherent traits of mission variability, collaborative interaction, and dynamic reconstruction pose escalating challenges in designing and verifying universal mass characteristics. This study examines the characteristics of clustered UAS and their alignment with universal quality attributes. It conducts an analysis and study of clustered UAS development and operation processes through model-based systems engineering (MBSE), employing demand decomposition and verification. Furthermore, it introduces a comprehensive MBSE-driven approach for designing universal quality characteristics, seamlessly integrating them into the system's functional and characteristic design processes across various developmental stages. Ultimately, this approach facilitates the realization of iterative, collaborative, and integrated design processes for universal quality characteristics within the MBSE framework.

articleTitle: Availability Analysis of Floating Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Availability, which has been the focus and research direction of the nuclear industry, is an important index for measuring the design and economy of nuclear power plants (NPPs). Further, it is one of the world association of nuclear operators indicators for NPP performance benchmarking. For large land-based commercial Pressurized Water Plant (PWR), certain requirements are given for the availability index by the American user requirements document and European user requirements; the calculation methods are relatively clear. However, there are a few standards and design requirement documents on the reliability for floating NPPs, in addition to the widely recognized methodology document for availability indicators calculation. In this paper, the analysis methodology of the availability of floating NPPs is provided by investigating the availability calculation methodology of land-based commercial NPPs and the characteristics of floating NPPs. A calculation model is built for certain floating NPPs to calculate the design availability factor in given scenarios. In addition, this paper presents the methods and approaches to optimize the availability index, which provides references for the general design optimization of floating NPPs.

articleTitle: Foreign Aerospace Improvement Maturity Model System to Aerospace Enterprises Quality Management System Evaluation and Improvement Work Inspiration
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The International Aerospace Quality Group (IAQG) has formulated an aerospace improvement maturity model system designed to assess and elevate the quality management system (QMS) within organizations. This framework enables aerospace entities to conduct self-assessments of their existing QMS structures, while also gauging their capacity for improvement. This paper primarily elucidates the model, methodology, and procedural aspects of this system and proffers pertinent recommendations tailored to the contemporary landscape of QMS evaluation and enhancement within aerospace enterprises in our nation.

articleTitle: Research on Sustainment Evaluation Technology for Ship Systems Based on Maturity Model
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: At present, ship systems are frequently exposed to support issues after delivery and use. The key reason is that the verification of support indicators and evaluation of support resources are generally considered during the system design and use stages. Even when the problems are identified, the technical status of the system cannot be modified at this time. To address the above issues, this article proposes a sustainment maturity level model suitable for China's ship system based on the research on sustainment maturity methods worldwide. The definition and connotation of each level are studied, and the evaluation criteria, evaluation items, and evaluation rules are developed for the entire life cycle of a ship system. The objective is to transform support validation evaluation from posterior to full life, full process, and refinement. This would promote the formation and maintenance of ship system support capabilities.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Based on the Slime Mold Algorithm under Imbalanced Data Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: With the rapid progress of technology, the application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has become widespread in various civilian and military activities. The research on fault diagnosis during a flight is a critical step towards enhancing the safety of UAV systems. Swarm-inspired heuristic algorithms have attracted significant attention owing to their fast iteration speed and strong optimization capabilities. This paper proposes a UAV fault diagnosis method based on the slime mold algorithm (SMA) under the condition of imbalanced data, thus addressing the issue of low diagnostic accuracy caused by a significantly longer normal flight time compared to the fault flight time in UAV operations. Using a real-world dataset of UAV flight faults with multiple fault patterns, the proposed approach optimizes the parameters of the support vector machine through SMA, thereby improving the fault diagnosis performance during actual UAV flights.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis of Emergency Escape Probability of Astronauts in Waiting-for-lift-offPhase
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: According to the characteristics of emergency escape system and process for astronauts in manned space launch missions, the analysis steps and quantitative analysis results of emergency escape probability for astronauts are presented. The research shows that the application of probabilistic risk analysis method can intuitively provide the key aspects of the astronaut emergency escape system in different stages of the mission and references for daily equipment maintenance management, plan formulation during the mission and command, and decision making in emergency situations.

articleTitle: Health State Recognition Technology for Complex Equipment Based on Mass Distance Entropy
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In view of the complexity of equipment working conditions, directly determining the health state using the direct monitoring signal, comprehensive utilization of Hilbert Huang transform (HHT) technology and the information entropy principle, a recognition method for complex equipment working condition based on mass distance entropy is proposed, and the test data of equipment in different states are used to verify the method. Based on the data of multi-part and multi-channel vibration signal measurement points of equipment, the health status division is carried out. Based on the study results, the proposed method can effectively divide the data samples of different health statuses, assess the effect of health status, identify working conditions, and provide support for the fine use of equipment.

articleTitle: Analysis of Current Trends of Comprehensive Support for Missiles' Solid Propellent-Based Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As one of the most important subsystems in missiles, comprehensive support for the solid power system plays a crucial role in the completion of the weapon work task. In view of the demand for modern ballistic weapons and combat modes for the comprehensive support capability of solid power systems, we analyzed the current situation and development trend of solid power system comprehensive support, provided suggestions to improve the comprehensive support level of solid power systems.

articleTitle: Theoretical Paradigm and Empirical Study of the General Quality Problem Closed-Loop Method: Insights from an International Case of Manned Flight Quality Issues
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The theoretical the core and difficult content of the general quality problem close loop method. This paper firstly analyzes the connotation of the concept of “theory”. Secondly, this paper draws lessons from Zachman Framework and combines with three layers including descriptive, explanatory and exploratory, which builds a three-dimensional space theory paradigm. Finally, this paper gives the empirical study of general quality problem close loop method and demonstrates its suitability based on a foreign case of manned flight quality problem.

Author Keywords: general quality problem close loop method

articleTitle: Exploration of Systems Engineering Fault Management Verification and Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Ensuring the safety of personnel and achieving success by proactively addressing and mitigating failures is a critical aspect of both domestic and international systems engineering endeavors. Effective fault management can guide, standardize, and enhance various tasks at the holistic engineering level. By verifying and validating fault management, the design and development cycle can effectively diagnose and forecast potential faults. Building upon a review and analysis of NASA's fault management efforts, this study delves into the scope, characteristic features, primary work content, and process of fault management verification and validation as applied to practical engineering tasks.

articleTitle: Human Factor Modeling and Risk Analysis Techniques in Space Launch Missions
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To address the practical problems of space launch missions, such as crew size, frequent state transitions, high work intensity, and pressure, human factor modeling and risk analysis technology are introduced. The classification of human error events and the applicable human factor reliability model in space launch mission are presented. With the example of hoisting tasks, the main processes of human factor modeling and risk analysis in launch missions are expounded. To provide support for improving the overall reliability of space launch missions.

articleTitle: Overview of NASA's Model-Based Systems Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper describes the development process of NASA's model-based systems engineering (MBSE) practice, which consists of the germination, exploratory, and extension practice periods. The future development direction of MBSE is represented by top-level strategies such as NASA Information Technology Strategic Plan, Future of Systems Engineering, and Future Model-Based Systems Engineering Vision. NASA released technical documents to standardize MBSE implementation and develop a model-based task assurance approach to promote quality assurance. NASA's typical MBSE practice, which includes the Europa Clipper Program and International Space Station Pilot Program, is recommended to provide reference for military enterprises and promote quality management in the MBSE environment.

articleTitle: High-Speed Fault Prognosis Approach and System of Industrial Intelligent Instruments
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Fault prediction is a crucial technology for the intelligent operation and maintenance management of equipment, and it plays a significant role in detecting equipment faults, minimizing the probability of faults, and improving operational efficiency. Although fault prediction technology has been widely applied in various fields, there is lack of prediction technology designed specifically for industrial intelligent instruments. The existing methods are complex and lack universality; therefore, this paper proposes a fault prognosis method and system for industrial intelligent instruments that is faster and lighter compared to the existing fault prediction methods. The proposed method is suitable for various types of industrial intelligent instruments and can continuously enhance prediction accuracy through feedback. Further, this method can partially supplement or replace the fault prediction process.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Design and Analysis Method of Network Cutting Separation Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Considering the phenomenon of detonation wave breaking and incomplete cutting during cutting and separation by wire cutting, the influence of the air gap on the detonation transmission performance of a network cutting separation mechanism was studied. A specific lapping module of the cutting system was designed, and finite element modeling and dynamic simulation of the cutting process were conducted. The detonation transmission and cutting process on various working conditions were simulated. The critical air gap thickness of the cutting cable that can be detonated reliably and wherein the detonation wave propagates stably is between 2.30 mm and 2.35 mm. Combined with the simulation results, the up-and-down test was carried out, and various lap models with different air gap thicknesses were designed. The reliable critical air gap thickness is approximately 2.38 mm. The reliability calculation results on different air gap thicknesses are presented. These provide theoretical and experimental support for the lap structure design and reliability analysis of the linear separation system.

articleTitle: Modeling Method for Testability Diagnostic Concept Based on SysML
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The existing methods for refining and decomposing testability design requirements suffer from limitations in effective tracking, confirmation, and implementation, along with issues pertaining to inaccurate interaction of testability design information. To address these shortcomings, this study devised a modeling method for testability diagnostic concepts utilizing systems modeling language (SysML). A standardized approach for designing elements of testability diagnostic concepts-including diagnostic scenarios, functions, and structures-is examined to facilitate the preliminary design of multilevel testability diagnostic concepts for various products. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through a systematic case study.

articleTitle: Investigation of Aerospace Product Standardization Leveraging Multidisciplinary Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: With the rapid growth of aerospace missions, the traditional model-customized scientific research mode can no longer adapt to the current situation of multitasking and high-density launches; thus, the productization of aerospace equipment is necessary. In this study, taking the transponder as an example, the multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO) method-starting from the source of product tasks-is used to optimize and unify the design parameters of the transponder. Finally, five universal products are formed that satisfy the selection requirements of most models. The general design of the transponder plays a key role in cost reduction and efficiency enhancement of the product, realizing the transformation from customized development oriented toward model requirements to small-batch production and off-the-shelf development oriented toward market requirements. This method will be applied to other aerospace products in the future.

articleTitle: Framework of Fatigue Crack Growth Life Monitoring for Nickel-Based Superalloy GH4169 Based on Thermodynamic Entropy Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: A framework to monitor the life of the fatigue crack growth (FCG) of the nickel-based superalloy GH4169 based on thermodynamic entropy generation is proposed in this paper. A finite element analysis method combined with ABAQUS and FRANC3D was established to simulate FCG behavior, and a Python program was written to calculate the entropy generation of the chosen thermodynamic system. The results illustrated that the fatigue fracture entropy (FFE) can be treated as a constant that is dependent on temperature. A damage model based on the degeneration-entropy generation theorem was proposed to estimate the life consumption in the FCG process. Finally, the FCG tests were used to compare the estimate from the damage model, and the results showed that this damage model can provide a reliable life monitor of FCG process.

articleTitle: Reliability Design Verification of High-Performance Broadband Radiofrequency Information-Processing Microsystems
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In response to the needs of fields such as intersatellite high-speed communication, relay bidirectional high-speed data transmission, ground data transmission, ground measurement and control, and comprehensive information processing, a series of key micro system technologies-namely, high-performance broadband radiofrequency (RF) information- processing microsystem architecture design, high-density packaging integration design of RF digital heterogeneous signals, and advanced micro system packaging technology-is being adopted. The purpose is to verify autonomous and controllable high-performance broadband RF information-processing microsystem products and usher in intelligent aerospace communication systems. Devising solutions to the bottleneck problem of localization and microminiaturization promoted the development and reformation of systems; led to wireless communication applications in multiple frequency bands and formats; fulfilled the application requirements of integrated information-processing platforms including onboard resource management, task scheduling, and computer multitasking; and satisfied the criteria for the new generation of aerospace engineering, which emphasizes high-performance real-time broadband RF information-processing miniaturization, as well as autonomous and controllable applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation of the Impact of Electrode R-Angle Design on the Electric Field in Multilayer Ceramic High-Voltage Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The conventional verification of capacitors entails a multitude of reliability tests, necessitating a substantial quantity of products and costly instrumentation. Consequently, the verification process is characterized by elevated costs and protracted cycles. To investigate the impact of the R-angle design in multilayer ceramic high-voltage capacitor electrodes on electric field distribution, an analysis of electromagnetic simulations was conducted. This analysis examined various R-angle designs within the wire mesh, discerning the influence of R-angle size and shape on electric field distribution. The simulation yielded insights into the relationships among different R-angle sizes, distinct R-angle shapes, and the size and distribution of the electric field.

articleTitle: 3300 V Planar Gate IGBT Devices with a Single-Zone Tapered Junction Termination Extension Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In this paper, a new terminal structure single-zone tapered junction termination extension (SZ-TJTE) is introduced and analyzed thoroughly using numerical device simulations. The proposed structure incorporates a single-zone junction termination extension (JTE) with a tapered junction outer edge, which can be fabricated conveniently using a graded implantation masking film. SZ-TJTE effectively alleviates the electric field concentration effect in termination. Compared with the single-zone JTE structure, the device utilizing the SZ-TJTE structure can significantly increase the window of ion implantation dose by 61.5% at the optimal angle, reduce the effective area of the device by 24.4%, and increase the breakdown voltage by 12.5% at the optimal dose.

articleTitle: Integrated Production Scheduling Based on Manufacturing System Resilience
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The high-quality development of equipment is firmly linked to the quality assurance of the production process. However, the research on utilizing the health prediction of manufacturing systems to guide production and operation decisions is insufficient. This is resulting in unnecessary production cost increases and product quality losses. Therefore, an integrated production scheduling method based on system resilience is proposed. First, a manufacturing system mission reliability model considering equipment performance and product quality is constructed. Second, the connotation and analysis method of system resilience are proposed based on mission reliability. Then, the initial production planning model and dynamic rescheduling model are established by considering mission reliability and system resilience as constraints, and the optimal production scheduling decisions are obtained by genetic algorithms. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using an example of a bogie manufacturing system.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of Maintenance System for Space Manipulator Grapple Fixture
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The space manipulator plays an integral role in the assembly and construction of the China space station. The grapple fixture is positioned at designated locations on the space station as the foundation for the space manipulator. It is utilized in conjunction with the space manipulator to capture target objects and complete crawling tasks. The performance of the space manipulator is directly impacted by the grapple fixture, and a failure of the grapple fixture can even jeopardize the space station mission. This paper analyzed the maintenance requirements of the grapple fixture, proposed a maintenance system for it, and executed replacement tasks with the assistance of maintenance tools and astronauts in orbit. The feasibility of this approach is verified through ground testing and simulation analysis. The results will serve as a valuable reference and engineering guidance for future space manipulator maintenance.

articleTitle: A Condition-Based Delay Maintenance Planning for Two-Stage Discrete Deterioration System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The maintenance cost comprises a large percentage of management cost in the whole life, and reasonable planning can significantly reduce this cost. This paper investigates delay-maintenance planning, within condition-based maintenance for a two-stage discrete degradation system. Specifically, 1) if the inspection times in the normal stage exceed a pre-defined limit, the system is replaced after a delay time; and 2) the system suffers a replacement after a defective-dependent delay time once the defective state is diagnosed. It should be noted that the inspection is unnecessary in two delay duration conditions. With this strategy, the remaining life is fully utilized, and excellent cost-savings is realized in the numerical experiment, which verifies the applicability and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Foreign Material Exclusion Management in Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This study aimed to address the critical issue of foreign material exclusion (FME) management in nuclear power plant maintenance activities, a domain wherein the presence of foreign materials poses significant risks to operational efficiency and nuclear safety. Confronting challenges such as low work efficiency, heightened risks in deviation management, and complications in tracking foreign materials, this study entailed a comprehensive examination of the FME organizational management and documentation systems in nuclear power plants, utilizing illustrative cases of typical foreign materials. Recommendations were formulated across various facets including preliminary preparation management, FME process management, area-specific foreign material management, foreign material event management, and over arching FME management protocols. Additionally, successful implementations of digital FME management devices were analyzed. By enhancing aspects such as process and tool management, this study sought to mitigate organizational, managerial, and technological shortcomings in foreign material prevention, subsequently decreasing the frequency of foreign material incidents and improving the efficiency of FME management protocols.

articleTitle: Automated Analysis Method for Software Failure Modes Based on Models and Data
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The primary purpose of software engineering is to provide high-quality software, aimed at reducing the amount of software failures. To increase the effectiveness and efficiency of an ordinary software failure-mode analysis, an automated software failure-mode analysis method is proposed. The automated method combines a model-based approach with historical data to overcome the limitations of the ordinary method. Furthermore, the extracting and matching algorithms that are employed in the automated analysis method are discussed. Feature space is used to obtain software failure mode features. The advantages of the automated method over the ordinary method are verified through engineering applications.

articleTitle: Abnormal Monitoring of the Complex Electromechanical System with the Improved Local Outlier Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Conventional methods cannot identify the local abnormal points of the dataset considering the large amounts data in the complex electromechanical system. In addition, points in the point group stray when mining exception events, and therefore, an improved local outlier detection method is proposed for incremental improvements in the local outlier detection algorithm. This method not only effectively increases the recalculation efficiency of large amounts of data in timely production but also solve outliers that help detect inaccurate problems that did not use any known system information. Simulation experiment results with the sample data in the TE process showed confirmed that different improvement methods were better, as confirmed with an example experiment showed that the proposed method has a large amount of data processing advantage and better abnormal monitoring ability.

articleTitle: Product Successful Data Envelopment Analysis Method and Risk Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In the process of quality inspection, the review of product performance and material process discreteness to determine whether it is within the scope of test assessment is crucial. In this study, the product performance and material process discreteness are enveloped in the scope of test review implementation measures. In other words, the data envelopment analysis, and its success is explained. This method mainly compares the product data to be analyzed with several product data successfully verified by testing to judge whether the product data to be analyzed falls within the scope of the envelope to evaluate whether the product has the ability to perform the task. This method can be used not only to evaluate the product performance, but also to analyze the discreteness of key parameters such as materials and processes. From the quality control viewpoint, product successful data enveloping analysis is an effective method to analyze the discreteness of key performance, material, and process parameters through statistical analysis based on prior information.

articleTitle: Accelerating Event-Driven Simulation for Dynamic Risk Analysis: A Dynamic Event Tree Method
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This study addresses the application and optimization of discrete dynamic event trees (DDETs) in the quantitative assessment of dynamic risk during the use phase of complex equipment systems and proposes a method for accelerating event-driven simulation of high-dimensional dynamic systems through dynamic event trees with neural differential equations. The dynamic system is constructed and described by neural event ordinary differential equations (ODEs)., Subsequently, the connection between DET and neural ODE is revealed. Based on this connection, we incorporate into the current context DET branching rules driven by intensity, event, and experience with several common termination rules as event functions. Finally, we validate the algorithm using a case of a study water tank.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Mission Reliability Modeling and Evaluation Method of System of Systems Based on Kill Chain Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Modern warfare is system of systems operations including multiple military branches. The system of systems is composed of multiple platforms cooperating with each other to jointly perform system of systems missions, which are usually divided into multiple stages. Due to different mission requirements in different stages, the correlation relationship between platforms in the system of systems is time-varying. Traditional modeling methods, such as reliability block diagram model, fault tree model, and GO model, find it difficult to model the time-varying correlation relationship. In the dynamic models, Markov model can not model dynamic correlation relationships between platforms within the system of systems. Petri net model is difficult to provide accurate evaluation results for complex systems. Therefore, in this paper, the Kill chain network model is established to simulate and model system of systems missions. Firstly, the system of systems is regarded as a network, and platforms are regarded as various nodes. Secondly, define the nodes and edges of the network, and conduct mission reliability model, including network structure modeling and network behavior modeling. Finally, define criteria for mission success and evaluate mission reliability using the Monte Carlo simulation method. The modeling and evaluation method of this paper has the following innovative points and advantages. Firstly, it can model time-varying correlation relationships between platforms for multi-stage mission. Secondly, compared to reliability block diagram model, which only provides one mission reliability value, the mission reliability evaluated by proposed method changes over time. This supports both reliability design and evaluation, as well as synchronous simulation evaluation of reality and the model.

Author Keywords: Multi-Stage Mission Reliability of The System of Systems

articleTitle: Research on Quality Management Methods of Complex Product Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper analyzes the characteristics and problems of complex product supply chain quality management when a large number of small and medium-sized enterprises are involved. Focusing on all the processes of a complex product supply chain, a method of complex product supply chain quality management is proposed from the perspectives of admission management, quality assurance requirement transmission, process quality supervision, and supplier relationship management.

articleTitle: Effect of Residual Stress After Reflow Soldering of Ball Grid Array Mixed Solder Joint on Thermal Cycling Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of residual stress after reflow soldering on the thermal cycling of a ball grid array (BGA). The devices were analyzed after thermal cycling using methods such as macroscopic morphology observation and microscopic structure evolution. The residual stress and strain of an Sn63Pb37/Sn3.0Ag0.5Cu mixed BGA structure were obtained by applying the reflow soldering temperature profile through finite element simulation. Subsequently, temperature cycling loads were applied to the BGA package model after reflow soldering. The thermal fatigue life of the BGA solder joints was predicted using the Darveaux fatigue model based on the strain energy damage. The results showed that considering the residual stress after reflow soldering in the simulation, the equivalent plastic strain was relatively large. The maximum stress was located at the corners where the solder joints contacted the PCB and chip. Microscopic cracks were formed on the interface at the chip-end in critical solder joints. The life prediction indicated that the relatively high residual stress generated during the reflow soldering process had negligible effect on the thermal fatigue performance of the hybrid BGA solder joints.

articleTitle: Improving the Partial Metallization Accuracy of Ceramic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper describes a method to improve the partial metallization accuracy of ceramic packaging. We describe the partial metallization process of ceramic packages, compare the metallization accuracy using a new process, and compare electrical parameters before and after using the new process. This technological process is easy to master and can be employed for large-scale production to ensure the quality and reliability of products in the same and different batches to effectively improve the first-pass yield.

articleTitle: Short-Circuit Behavior of 1200 V SiC MOSFETs at Different DC Power Supply Voltages
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Among the many failure mechanisms, short circuit is one of the failure modes that can cause permanent failure of switching devices. This study aimed to evaluate the short-circuit capability of low on-resistance SiC MOSFET power devices in hard-switching fault environments by conducting single pulse tests under various DC bus voltages. A batch of 1200 V low on-resistance SiC MOSFET power devices was tested under identical process conditions. The static characteristics of the devices at different moments were evaluated, and the failure phenomena were analyzed. The objective was to determine the different failure phenomena and regions occurring when devices fail at different DC voltages. As the DC voltage increased, the SiC MOSFET short-circuit failure mode gradually transitioned from delayed failure to direct failure at the time of failure and from gate source short-circuit failure to thermal runaway failure. Furthermore, the sequence of four short-circuit failure modes was determined to further narrow down the short-circuit safe operating area and help optimize the SiC MOSFET device performance in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Quantitative Reliability Analysis of Detonating Fuse Based on AHP
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As a key component in the design of a linear separation device, the design reliability level of a detonating cable directly affects the separation success or failure of the separation body. This study proposes the analytic hierarchy method theory to perform a combined quantitative analysis of the environmental elements and key design parameters affecting the reliability of the detonating cable. The results are expected to help improve the inherent reliability level of the detonating cable, determine the key environmental design influencing factors and key design parameters of the detonating cable design, lay the foundation for reliability design, and merge functional performance design.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Integrated Modular Avionics Based on Multi-State System with Performance Sharing Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To solve the problem of reliability modeling and evaluation of integrated modular avionics (IMA), this study extends the multi-state system with common bus performance sharing based on the stricture and work principles of IMA. Subsequently, based on the extended model, the universal generating function is applied to evaluate the reliability of IMA. Finally, a case study on the integrated task processing system in IMA is used to analyze the impact of changes in the number of spare general processing units on system reliability, with the aim is to validate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on the Design of a Data Recorder for Human Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In this paper, the research methods of reliability physics, human reliability, psychology, and management science, such as worst-case analysis, failure mode and effect analysis, and Human reliability analysis are investigated. Subsequently, the key factors of the human reliability of a data recorder are determined, and the human factor error is analyzed. In addition, a human reliability model of the systems is established, and an improvement scheme for human reliability analysis is proposed through empirical research. The design improvement suggestions and further research direction of human reliability are also discussed.

articleTitle: Research on System Reliability Model Considering Resource Sharing and Reconfiguration Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To analyze the reliability of a system through a resource-sharing reconfiguration strategy, a reliability modeling method of resource-sharing reconfiguration mechanism based on the dynamic fault tree (DFT) is proposed. Based on the conventional fault tree, the SR logic gate is introduced to construct a DFT model corresponding to the shared reconfiguration mechanism of unidirectional resource sharing reconfiguration, bidirectional resource sharing reconfiguration, and single/bidirectional complex sharing reconfiguration. Subsequently, the model is solved by the Monte Carlo simulation method to address configuration variations before and after resource-sharing reconstruction. Finally, considering an avionics system as an example, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Fault Information Mining in Avionics Components Based on Unstructured Data
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To address the requirements of unstructured fault data mining and statistical analysis of avionics systems, this study excavates implicit knowledge, investigates potential knowledge associations, and realizes a deep understanding of knowledge to better interpret data. Combined with recent progress of text data extraction technology, this paper studies the entity relationship extraction and failure time statistical method based on attention-based bidirectional long short-term memory to realize the statistical analysis of failure time law of components. In this study, 413 cases of unstructured fault data of avionics system components were collected, and the entity relationship extraction and failure statistical methods proposed in this paper were verified and analyzed. The results showed that the components would have a high probability of failure within 10,000 hours of each flight, and the number and time of multi-function control display failures were high. This paper proposes an unstructured data analysis method for avionics systems, which can provide a reference for a maintenance engineer, provide a basis for the management decision-making of avionics maintenance institutions, and improve the maintenance quality of avionics systems.

articleTitle: Weakness Analysis and Common Medium of Ludd Vehicle Based on “1+3+5” Principle
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This study developed a comprehensive method in response to the variety of existing analytical methods targeting the weak links in launch vehicles. This method integrates weak link identification, control mechanisms, and closed-loop confirmation. The procedural steps for implementing this method have been elucidated, in conjunction with its application to typical launch vehicle products. Consequently, the approach enhances both the effectiveness and relevance of single-point product reliability design, as well as the efficiency of overall product reliability assurance.

articleTitle: Reliability Prediction of COTS Electronic Components: An Enhanced FIDES Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) electronic components present a compelling technological option owing to their cost-effectiveness, while simultaneously introducing a significant reliability concern when integrated into military or aerospace systems. The reliability prediction plays a pivotal role in evaluating system dependability and potential failure risks before the assembly of equipment. To enhance the accuracy of predicting the reliability of COTS electronic components, this study devised an improved FIDES reliability prediction methodology. This enhanced approach incorporates a refined physics-of-failure (PoF) model and fundamental failure rates specific to integrated circuits. A case analysis focused on the application of COTS components within microsatellites was also performed. This study aimed to examine the diverse failure rates associated with COTS components operating under various profiles. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed methodology was assessed by evaluating the outcomes of these reliability predictions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Analysis of 1.2 kV SiC JBS Diodes with High Performance and Avalanche Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In this study, a 1.2 KV SiC JBS diode with a current spreading layer (CSL) is designed.
