It is observed that the forward conduction characteristics of the device are enhanced substantially compared with the conventional JBS by decreasing the specific on-resistance effectively when the reverse breakdown voltage can still satisfy the requirement of 1.2 KV. Additionally, the avalanche capability of JBS diodes with different CSL doping concentrations is studied further. It is observed that the avalanche current is transferred from the terminal region with a smaller area to the active region with a larger area because the addition of the CSL structure increases the electric field strength in the active region. Moreover, with the increase in doping concentration, the electric field strength in the source region is enhanced. This results in an increase in the avalanche current flowing from the active region. This, in turn, effectively suppresses the maximum temperature of the current-sensitive terminal region. It is demonstrated that the maximum temperature of the CSL structure decreases by 53.8% compared with that of the conventional JBS structure. Therefore, it is inferred that the CSL structure is an effective solution to improve the avalanche capability of 4H-SiC JBS diode.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Dynamic On-resistance and Switching Performance of Cascode GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The dynamic on-resistance degradation and switching performance of a commercial 650 V cascode GaN power device are evaluated. A double-pulse test platform is used to investigate the dynamic on-resistance behaviors with various off-state drain bias voltages, drain currents, and off-state stress times under hard-switching conditions. To evaluate switching performance, an Si-based metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) is used as a reference for comparing dynamic on-resistance and switching energy loss with cascode GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMT). The test results indicate that higher off-state drain bias and drain current lead to more severe dynamic on-resistance degradation. Moreover, with a higher switching speed, the cascode GaN HEMT demonstrates a reduced switching energy loss compared to that of the Si-based MOSFET.

Index Terms: Gallium Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Assessment of Organic Coating Based on Three-stage Degradation Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The degradation of coating properties directly affects the potential for corrosion on ships. Numerous studies have focused on stochastic degradation modeling and the mechanisms of coating degradation. However, there is a lack of methods that integrate both aspects into a unified degradation modeling framework. Through an analysis of the degradation mechanism, we have divided coating degradation into three stages: the smooth, fast, and slow degradation periods. Based on the three-stage degradation characteristics, we propose a three-stage Wiener process remaining useful life prediction model. The experimental results show that the proposed model can effectively explain the coating degradation process, and exhibit favorable prediction results.

articleTitle: Reliability Index Distribution System of Liquid Attitude and Orbit Control Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To satisfy the engineering requirements for the reliability design of liquid attitude and orbit control power propulsion systems, this paper proposes a framework to model the reliability and analyze the design of liquid attitude and divert control propulsion systems. Based on methods such as system analysis and failure mode and effects analysis, the proposed framework integrates the commonly used reliability design methods to satisfy the needs of engine reliability design. A four-layer client-server architecture is adopted to describe the functional composition of the system. This architecture enables reliability design collaboration between the system/component design departments of attitude and orbit control power propulsion systems, within a distributed network operation environment. Moreover, open database connectivity is used to establish connections with the external design systems. Data sharing and transmission are performed to synchronize the reliability design of the attitude and orbit control power propulsion system with the functional and structural designs. Lastly, the structure of the engine reliability information database and relationship between the database forms are identified.

Author Keywords: liquid attitude and orbit control power system

articleTitle: Research on Small Sample Quality Analysis Method for Aerospace Products
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This study focuses on the high complexity, multibatch, and small-batch characteristics of aerospace products. The applicability, reliability, and uncertainty evaluation methods of small sample indicators are used to analyze and evaluate the defect rate of these products. By integrating prior information from multiple product batches, error correction is performed on the single batch and small sample defect rate data to enhance the accuracy of defect rate calculations. The objective is to identify weak links and defects in the production process, identify and address systemic quality hazards, support product improvements, and mitigate losses through the small sample quality analysis method.

articleTitle: Failure Mechanism and New Technique of Junction Termination Extension Under Pulsed Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical analysis of the degradation mechanism of Junction Termination Extension (JTE) terminals under pulsed stress. The incomplete depletion of JTE terminals leads to its functional degradation. The accuracy of the theoretical analysis was verified by simulation. Based on theoretical analysis, this paper develops a method to increase the avalanche breakdown voltage of JTE terminal devices under pulsed stress. Simulation results show that the device's breakdown voltage under pulsed stress of 2 kV/ns can be increased from 661 to 1486 V using the designed dynamic JTE. Mixed JTE devices comprising static and dynamic JTE show a significant increase in breakdown voltage over the pulsed stress interval of 0 to 2 kV/ns compared to the previous. This study contributes to improving the reliability of JTE terminal devices under pulsed stress and is expected to expand the application of JTE terminals in pulsed power devices.

articleTitle: Index System for Evaluating Helicopters' General Quality Characteristics Under Digital Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The evaluation index system serves as the fundamental and pivotal component of the assessment of general quality characteristics in helicopters. This paper focuses on the establishment of such an evaluation index system. It involves an analysis of the interrelationships among the evaluation indices for general quality characteristics. Additionally, it outlines the principles guiding the establishment of this index system, ultimately resulting in the formulation of an index system tailored to the evaluation of helicopters' general quality characteristics under digital conditions. This index system holds significant reference value for related endeavors in the field.

articleTitle: Research on Cross-Condition and Cross-Equipment Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Adversarial Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Transfer learning (TL) is being gradually applied to the field of equipment fault diagnosis. TL can use the diagnostic knowledge learned from a source domain to solve the diagnosis problem of a target domain, which is expected to solve the few-shot problem in fault diagnosis. The existing fault diagnosis methods based on TL are mainly aimed at cross- condition transfer fault diagnosis. For cross-equipment transfer problems, most existing transfer methods cannot be used owing to the large data distribution offset. To address this issue, this research introduces a fault diagnosis method that utilizes adversarial TL. Adversarial TL is a method that combines TL with the concept of a generative adversarial network. First, a domain-shared convolutional neural network is established to extract fault features. The feature distributions extracted from the source and target domains are aligned by the adversarial training method. Finally, the fault category is identified. The fault diagnosis method is validated using a publicly available dataset. The results indicate that the method can extract features suitable for cross-condition and cross-equipment transfer fault diagnosis and enhance the precision of intelligent diagnostic models.

articleTitle: Software System Testing Technology for Ship Information Systems Based on Performance Experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Based on the attributes of a ship information system and in consideration of software system testing requirements and challenges, this study explores performance testing techniques for ship information systems. It delves into content, capabilities, and practical applications of software system testing in this context.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis Technology for Aircraft Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: A fault analysis method for aircraft equipment is proposed to meet the requirements of flight reliability, high safety, and low support costs, and the key technologies involved in the method are studied. A Kalman filter is used to preprocess flight data. Using the improved spectrum temporal graph neural network, the system fault analysis method based on data drive is studied, and build an aircraft equipment fault analysis platform. Taking an air-conditioning system with a high failure rate in civil aviation airliners as an example, the effectiveness of the system is verified. This study provides a new idea for aircraft fault analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Life-cycle Reliability and Component Importance of Propeller Pitch Control System using Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Propeller pitch control systems have complex structures with various components that participate in different task stages. In this study, a fault tree analysis model and multistage Bayesian network are used to qualitatively and quantitatively analyze the importance of these components and calculate the changes in system reliability. First, the fault tree analysis model of each stage is established according to system components. On this basis, the importance of each component is qualitatively analyzed. Next, the fault tree model is transformed into a Bayesian network model for reliability analysis and the quantitative analysis of importance. The changes in the reliability and importance of each unit during the operation of the pitch control system are obtained. The system reliability after 400 h of operation is 0.982. The components with high importance in the system are the motor, carbon brushes, and circuit connections. Protective measures are proposed to provide technical support for the safe operation of the propeller pitch control system.

articleTitle: A Rapid Analysis Method for VME Bus Transaction Function in Open-Source IP Cores Based on Signal Transition Graph Model
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The adoption of open-source IP cores in System on Chip (SoC) design requires more effort in analyzing, understanding, and evaluating function verification, which is less convenient than proprietary closed-source IP cores due to the increasing complexity of IP core structures. This study proposes a signal transition graph (STG)-based function verification method for VersaModule Eurocard (VME) bus transactions of an open-source peripheral component interconnect express (PCIe) - VME bridge IP core to reduce verification time. First, the behavior of VME bus transactions defined in the VME64x standard specification is mapped to a reference STG model. Next, the implementation of bus transactions in the open-source IP core code is mapped to a code implementation STG model. Subsequently, a comparative analysis is conducted between the code implementation STG and the reference STG. Finally, an assessment is made to determine the function compliance of the open-source IP core with the VME64x standard in terms of implementing VME bus functions. The results show that the key read transaction transfer and write transaction transfer function implementations of the VME side in the IP core are essentially consistent with the requirements specified in the standard using the proposed function equivalence checking method. This demonstrates the applicability of the proposed methodology for swiftly verifying the correctness of VME transaction function implementation.

articleTitle: Vector Characterization Method of Multiple Stress Acceleration Factors for High-Reliability Electronic Products
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Accelerated life testing is one of the rapid verification methods for highly reliable electronic products in complex service environments. Existing acceleration models primarily rely on single or double stress, making it difficult to meet the reliability improvement needs of highly reliable electronic products in terms of fault excitation efficiency and service environment simulation accuracy. This article proposes a vector representation method for the multi stress acceleration factor of highly reliable electronic products based on the random vector theory and product failure time model, considering the multi stress coupling effect in the product failure mechanism to improve the accuracy of the multi stress acceleration model when describing the product failure mechanism. The method was applied to statistically analyze the temperature, humidity, and electrical stress constant acceleration life test data of power control components under 5 different stress combinations. The predicted results of the model showed an error of less than 10% compared to the test results, verifying the scientific and feasible vector characterization of multi stress acceleration factors in highly reliable electronic products and providing a method for the research of multi stress acceleration test technology in electronic products.

articleTitle: GCPAT-Based Fault Diagnosis Method for Asynchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In this paper, a fault diagnosis method based on GCPAT is proposed. Firstly, the vibration signal is converted into a symmetrical snowflake image. Firstly, the vibration signal is converted into a symmetrical snowflake image by using the symmetric point pattern (SDP) method. Secondly, the simple linear iterative clustering (SLIC) method is used to take the isomorphic superpixels in the SDP image as nodes to form the graph according to the color, texture, and distance features. The results show that GCPAT can effectively improve the accuracy of fault diagnosis and provide good reference value The results show that GCPAT can effectively improve the accuracy of fault diagnosis and provide a good reference value for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation Method for Telemetry, Tracking and Command Communication of Space Station on Multi-Mission Arcs
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In manned space missions, the reliability of the measurement and control system is essential for the normal operation of spacecraft and safety of astronauts. Based on the analysis of different mission profiles of space station, the reliability model of the spacecraft telemetry, tracking, and command (TT&C) system based on mission arcs is established, and the evaluation method of TT&C communication reliability for different mission arcs proposed. Through the reliability analysis of each TT&C task, a method for organizing each TT&C task is obtained. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified through the on-orbit verification of different mission arcs of the space station.

articleTitle: Four Two-Parameter Distributions for Substitution of the Three-Parameter Weibull Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The three-parameter Weibull distribution (3PWD) has been widely used as a fatigue life or material strength model. As its support depends on the location parameter, the maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters are sometimes nonexistent or biased. This is particularly true when the sample is small, or/and the data are incomplete. Although the maximum product of spacing method and its variants have been developed to address this issue, they are not always efficient. Thus, this study proposes a new approach to thoroughly solve this problem. The basic idea is to use a two-parameter distribution with a light left tail to substitute the 3PWD. Four such distributions have been identified: lognormal, inverse Gaussian, Birnbaum-Saunders and maximum Gumbel distributions. The main advantages of the proposed approach are the following: There is no need to estimate a location parameter, and the model is simpler. A numerical experiment is carried out, and two real-world examples are included to validate the proposed approach and its appropriateness.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of human-machine systems based on Hybrid Causal Logic model and Cognitive Reliability and Error Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Accident evolution in human-machine systems is a complex process, often influenced by multiple factors and characterized by uncertainty. This paper proposes a risk assessment method for human-machine systems based on the Hybrid Causal Logic (HCL) model and Cognitive Reliability and Error Analysis Method (CREAM). The HCL model is a three-layer structure which incorporates Event Tree (ET), Fault Tree (FT), and Bayesian Network (BN). The ET-FT considers the impact of machine failures and human errors. In addition, this study also uses the BN to describe the common cause effect of Common Performance Conditions (CPCs) on multiple human error modes. Therefore, we employ CREAM to quantify human errors, and utilize a Binary Decision Diagram (BDD) algorithm to rank the importance measures of each event and calculate the accident probability of the risk scenario. We present a case study of a twin-engine aircraft experiencing a one-sided engine fire and apply the ET-FT-BN framework to model the risk scenario. We calculate the important measures and accident probability, thereby demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method. This paper provides a scientific and effective analysis tool for risk assessment of human-machine system.

articleTitle: Vibration Environment Prediction for Complex Structures with Interval Uncertain Elastic Joints
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper presents a new method that uses a frequency response function based sub-structuring method (FBSM) and an interval factor method (IFM), i.e., FBS-IFM, for predicting the vibration environment of complex structures with interval uncertain elastic joints. The FBSM is reformulated based on the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury formula and singular value decomposition to overcome the bottleneck related to the invalidity of the existing FBSM for a singular impedance matrix of elastic joints. The distribution interval of the FRF amplitude is achieved with IFM using a massless spatial beam element with an interval uncertain elastic modulus and damping coefficient to simulate the interval uncertain elastic joints. Finally, the proposed FBS-IFM is built and is verified by comparing the corresponding calculation results with the Monte Carlo simulation method of a designed simulation structure. All results illustrate that the proposed FBS-IFM achieves high efficiency.

articleTitle: Trust State Monitoring of Human-Machine Co-Driving Based on EEG Signals in Intelligent Driving Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The rapid development and widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology are reshaping the dynamics of human-machine interaction. Intelligent driving, as a prominent representative of the latest technological revolution, achieves precise control over driving tasks through collaboration between the driver and AI systems. In this context, the driver's trust in AI plays a pivotal role in influencing the efficiency of human-machine cooperation and overall driving safety in intelligent driving scenarios. Nonetheless, there remains a notable absence of methods for accurately assessing and monitoring the state of human-machine interaction, particularly with regard to trust levels during co-driving. To address this gap, this study established an experimental platform utilizing UC-win/road software and conducted experiments to capture and analyze the driver's EEG signals. The primary objective was to develop a neural network-based trust discrimination model. This model exhibits a remarkable level of accuracy, achieving a data analysis accuracy rate of 90%. Furthermore, the research findings indicate that electrodes positioned in the occipital region of the brain exhibit heightened sensitivity to variations in human-machine trust levels compared to other electrodes. Notably, a trust discrimination model constructed solely using these occipital electrodes achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 98.52%. The significance of this trust discrimination model lies in its potential to dynamically measure human-machine trust levels, enabling real-time predictions and early warnings regarding AI interaction risks in intelligent driving scenarios.

articleTitle: Human Reliability Modeling Method of Phased-Mission Systems Considering the Cumulative Effects of Performance Shaping Factors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Existing researches on reliability modeling for phased-mission systems (PMSs) have predominantly focused on analyzing failure dependencies within machinery. However, there has been limited exploration into human reliability modeling within these systems, with a particular dearth of attention to the cumulative impacts of performance shaping factors (PSFs). Consequently, this study introduces an innovative human reliability modeling approach for PMSs that explicitly accounts for the cumulative effects of PSFs. From the perspective of situation awareness formation, Bayesian network (BN) is adopted to model the human cognition reliability during the multi-phase mission. Fatigue and stress are recognized as two significant PSFs that accumulate over time. To represent these accumulative effects, this paper employs two time-varying models, integrating them into the BN framework using fuzzy methods. Furthermore, the phase dependencies of cognitive activities are classified into two distinct effects: the promoting effect and the inhibiting effect of human error, which are quantified probabilistically using a human reliability analysis method. Finally, the proposed method is exemplified with a three-phase detection mission of ground combat vehicle.

articleTitle: Flink-Stream-Computing-Driven Parallel Particle Filter for the Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Facilities
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: With the advent and development of big data technology, advanced stream computing represented by Flink has demonstrated significant application value in the condition monitoring of industrial facilities. In recent years, particle filter (PF) technology has been extensively applied to time series data prediction and has demonstrated superiority in nonlinear and nonGaussian systems. When undertaking the predictive maintenance of industrial facilities, stream computing must be conducted on the continuously emerging data of facilities to dynamically predict the key performance indices at any future time. However, the fusion application of a PF and big data stream computing has no precedent. Thus, this study proposes a parallel PF method driven by Flink stream computing for real-time prognostics of facilities. The main contributions of this study include: 1) execution of parallel online modeling of time series data through Flink, as well as periodic autonomous generation of prognostic models, and 2) embedding of the update and prediction processes of the PF into the Flink stream computing program to improve the PF efficiency in practical industrial applications. The monitoring data streams for multiple facilities are simulated through Kafka to test the functionality and performance of the parallel PF. Modeling tasks are periodically triggered and followed closely with the prediction results output by the PF, with operation under parallel mode for all the facilities. The relative prediction error is less than 1.9%. Further, the average lag between the output time of the prediction results and event time triggering modeling is 3.6 s, and the average execution time of the PF computing tasks is 90 ms.

articleTitle: Study on the Failure Mechanism and Reliability Evaluation of Space Capture Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The space capture device is an important part of the launch vehicle, particularly in the task of separating the satellite from the rocket. Failure to securely engage the docking bolt in the device may have severe consequences for the subsequent launch mission, potentially resulting in mission failure. This study focuses on investigating the space capture device as its research subject. The analysis centers on understanding the functional principles of the capture device, identifying causes of failure, and delineating primary failure modes. Moreover, it establishes failure criteria, considering aspects such as energy, rebound velocity, and interference area. The paper formulates a reliability mathematical model for the capture device through theoretical derivation and the application of the response surface method. This model facilitates the assessment of the capture device's reliability and the evaluation of how various parameters influence its reliability. The findings indicate that, when accounting for the failure mode where the docking bolt fails to pass through the bushing, the capture does not fail if the velocity of the docking bolt closely aligns with the assumed mean speed. Consequently, the analysis focuses solely on the failure mode involving the docking bolt passing through the bushing and subsequently bouncing back through it. Utilizing the series reliability model established based on rebound speed and interference area, the calculated failure probability is determined to be 0.00052. Notably, the projection length of the bush reed on the bolt and the friction coefficient between the docking bolt and the bushing emerge as the two factors exerting the most substantial influence on the capture device's failure probability. An increase in the probability of successful capture can be achieved by appropriately increasing the projection length of the bush reed on the bolt while simultaneously reducing the friction coefficient between the docking bolt and the bushing.

articleTitle: Quality Supervision Method for Aerospace Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To ensure both the quality and timeliness of aerospace projects conform to engineering standards, this study investigated mature quality supervision methodologies from diverse engineering disciplines for potential applicability in aerospace projects. Based on supervision techniques from the International Federation of Consulting Engineers and international satellite product assurance methods, the study synthesized key insights and lessons from advanced international quality supervision practices. According to the unique attributes of aerospace project development and testing procedures, this study devised a comprehensive framework for quality supervision, encompassing organizational models, workflow processes, and principal supervision components. This framework serves as a referential guide for implementing quality supervision initiatives within the aerospace sector.

articleTitle: Reliability Model of Ion Thrusters Considering Competing Failure
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of reliability evaluation for ion thrusters, the degradation distribution model and weighted least square method combined with the E-Bayes distribution curve model are respectively constructed based on the assumption of failure mode independence. Considering the conditions of Weibull distribution, life distribution parameters are fitted to obtain the reliability indexes' point and interval estimation. Subsequently, the robustness of the model and the superiority of the method are discussed with an example, which shows the value of the method in second-process applications.

articleTitle: Survivability Design and Resilience Analysis of Equipment System-of-Systems Based on Resilience Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The equipment system-of-systems (ESoS) plays a crucial role in national defense strategy. Given the myriad challenges that ESoS encounters and the potentially dire consequences of reduced survivability in battlefield scenarios, it is imperative to mitigate the impact of disturbances through effective survivability design. This article outlines a comprehensive approach for ESoS lifecycle survivability design, drawing upon resilience theory. This approach encompasses four key stages: safe protection, reliable operation, effective defense, and emergency recovery. To evaluate ESoS survivability within this framework, a hierarchical analysis is employed. Additionally, we delve into the causal relationships among various indicators at different levels of the survivability evaluation framework. We construct a system dynamics model to assess the resilience of ESoS systematically. To illustrate the application of these principles, we present a case study demonstrating the survivability design and resilience analysis of a specific ESoS. The findings reveal a remarkable 194 8% improvement in ESoS resilience against enemy attacks through the implementation of survivability design. Notably, among the four survivability stages, effective defense exerts the most significant influence on enhancing ESoS resilience, followed by safe protection, whereas emergency recovery and reliable operation have comparatively smaller impacts. The proposed survivability design methodology serves as a valuable guide for enhancing the lifecycle survivability of diverse ESoS. Additionally, the resilience evaluation approach we present can validate the effectiveness of survivability designs across various ESoS contexts.

articleTitle: Availability Improvement Technology of BeiDou Navigation Satellite
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In light of the significant demand for continuous service to global users, ensuring and improving constellation availability is a major challenge in the development and operation of the BeiDou navigation constellation. This paper focuses on the technical solutions to four key problems. For constellation development, a quantitative verification method for satellite availability using outage tree analysis is proposed, and a quantitative determination and improvement approach for weak points of availability is developed using outage effect analysis and a hazard time model. For constellation operation and maintenance, a constellation availability assessment method based on real-time data is proposed to control long-term outage risk, and an orbit control strategy with extended orbit control interval constraints is proposed to reduce scheduled outage risk. Additionally, an anomaly disposal process is optimized to reduce short-term anomaly risk, and a dynamic temperature control method, on-orbit reconstruction, and compensation strategy are proposed to extend the satellite's lifetime. These methods have been applied to the development and operation of the BeiDou navigation constellation, and the number and duration of satellite outages were found to decrease significantly, resulting in major economic and social benefits.

articleTitle: A Reliability Evaluation Model for High- Torque Density Motors Based on Markov Chain
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: In this study, Markov chains are used to divide and model the failure modes of high-torque density motors and obtain a reliability evaluation model for the same. Thermal path method was used to verify the internal stress field of the motor, thereby laying the foundation for reliability evaluation. Furthermore, the changes in motor reliability under different torque densities were investigated. Finally, the optimization method for installing heat pipes and winding sealing is applied to high-torque density motors to enhance their reliability.

articleTitle: A Dual-Branch Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Spatial Variable Scale Pooling for Inter-Class Incomplete Data
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The intelligent fault diagnosis method based on convolutional neural network (CNN) has achieved significant success in the field of mechanical fault diagnosis. However, its application has been limited to complete inter-class data obtained from controlled laboratory settings. In practical working scenarios, inter-class data often lacks sufficient fault data compared with health data, which leads to an unsatisfactory CNN performance. This paper proposes a dual-branch intelligent fault diagnosis method based on spatial variable scale pooling aiming at the constraint of CNN in capturing local features only to enhance the applicability of intelligent fault diagnosis methods in real working conditions and improve the fault feature representation capability and diagnostic accuracy. First, this method constructs a dual-branch model that combines the VGG16 convolutional network and the self-attention Encoder from the Transformer architecture, enabling the fusion of local and global features and enhancing the fault representation learning capability of the model. Second, the pooling layers within the convolutional branch are improved by introducing spatial variable scale pooling for extracting more detailed fault features. Finally, a fusion module is designed to align the extracted features from the dual-branch model semantically. The superiority of the proposed model is demonstrated through the experiment.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Digital Twin for Frontline Maintenance Support of Aviation Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As the core tool of digital construction in all walks of life, digital twin technology would play a key role in the transformation of the aviation equipment maintenance support field. By analyzing the business process of aviation equipment frontline maintenance support, systematically analyze the business functional requirements faced by the digital twin of aviation frontline equipment maintenance support; According to the 5-dimensional model of the digital twin, from the perspective of a physical entity, virtual entity, service, data and connection, the overall architecture of the digital twin of equipment maintenance support is proposed. Along the technical maturity level requirements of the digital twin, the specific methods to realize the digital twin of aviation equipment maintenance support are proposed from four aspects: digital definition, information interaction, model enabling and platform support. Finally, taking a typical grassroots maintenance workshop as an example, the results of the built maintenance support digital twin are presented, and the specific effects of typical functions are given. The business requirements, technical framework and implementation ideas can provide some reference for the Digital transformation of equipment maintenance support. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Using GNN Through Adversarial Attack
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of high-speed trains (HST) has underscored the escalating significance of ensuring the reliability and safety of HST braking systems. In recent years, data-driven fault diagnosis methods have gained traction, owing to the proliferation of sensors employed in fault diagnosis within this domain. Concurrently, fault diagnosis techniques rooted in causal and graph neural networks (GNN) have been gradually integrated into practice. Nevertheless, sensor errors pose significant challenges in the generation of causal graphs. Additionally, the presence of unbalanced data can lead to a deterioration in model performance when classifying minor sample categories. In response, we present an innovative approach for GNN-based fault diagnosis, incorporating adversarial attacks. In this study, we meticulously consider four distinct adversarial attack scenarios, encompassing all potential instances where errors may impact the data. Furthermore, we introduce adversarial regularization to uphold the method's integrity. To substantiate our approach, we conduct fault diagnosis experiments employing graph convolution networks (GCN) and graph attention networks (GAT) models on authentic datasets obtained from HST braking systems. Our empirical findings substantiate the efficacy of our adversarial attack method, which notably enhances the performance of the GNN model in addressing classification issues pertaining to unbalanced fault data.

articleTitle: Risk-Informed Performance and Safety Significance Analysis of NPP Mitigating Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Risk-informed regulation directs regulatory focus toward issues based on their level of risk significance. This approach integrates operating experience, accident analysis, risk assessment, and defense-in-depth philosophy into the decision-making process. The ultimate goal is to establish appropriate regulations that enhance safety within the nuclear industry without compromising it. This study draws upon inspection findings from nuclear power plants and employs the mitigating system performance indicator (MSPI) and the significance determination process (SDP) for its research. The study delves into the correlation and distinctions between MSPI and SDP, examining them from the perspectives of fundamental theory, risk analysis, and considerations for regulatory application. This study therefore serves as a valuable reference for the application and promotion of risk-informed regulatory approaches.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Optimal Design of Metal Indoor Corrosion Tests Based on Equivalence Degree of Corrosion Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The prevalent indoor corrosion test design methods commonly overlook the impact of environmental stress levels on the equivalence of corrosion mechanisms. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel indoor corrosion test design method based on corrosion mechanism equivalence, with the aim of enhancing the precision of simulating accelerated corrosion environments indoors. This enhancement is achieved by aligning the degradation mechanisms observed during material corrosion processes with those experienced in authentic environmental settings. To operationalize this approach, we introduce the concept of corrosion mechanism equivalence, quantified as the corrosion mechanism equivalence degree (CMed). Subsequently, we adapt conventional link function models to account for the probability distribution of environmental factors, thus facilitating accurate estimation of corrosion model parameters. Lastly, we formulate an optimization problem for accelerated corrosion testing based on CMed, incorporating constraints pertaining to environmental stress levels and acceleration factors. Illustrating the efficacy of this method is a real-world example, which demonstrates its ability to accurately simulate the actual material service environment. This is achieved by determining stress levels within indoor accelerated corrosion environments, all while ensuring the attainment of prescribed acceleration factors and corrosion mechanism equivalence.

articleTitle: Coupling Analysis of Mechanism Fatigue Wear in Vibration-Thermal Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The aircraft drag-parachute mechanism is key to ensuring the smooth deployment of the parachute. It is of great significance to study its damage evolution for aircraft landing safety. To simulate the time-varying damage of this mechanism under a vibration-thermal environment, a modeling method is proposed. The method considers the coupling between fatigue damage and fretting wear and introduces the local friction temperature rise on the contact surface of the study object. The influence of the two phenomena, the morphologic evolution of the contact surface with different slip types, and the problem of motion stuck are studied. The results show that, when considering the coupling influences of friction temperature increase and fatigue damage on wear, the friction force in the case of gross slip is mostly unchanged, whereas that in the case of partial slip increases significantly. In the second case, compared with the calculation of friction force that ignores the influences of both phenomena, when considering the coupling influence of friction temperature increase or fatigue damage on wear, the friction force on the contact surface increases by approximately 6.7%. However, when considering the combined coupling influence, it increases by approximately 20 %. Therefore, omitting the combined coupling influence reduces the prediction result of mechanism stuck failure probability smaller.

articleTitle: System Design and Characteristic Analysis of Manned Lunar Landing Spacecraft Based on SysML
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Considering the complexities of manned lunar exploration missions, i.e., multiple flight stages, complex vehicle statuses, and elevated reliability and safety criteria, this study undertakes a comprehensive design and characteristics analysis of the manned lunar exploration spacecraft system using the systems modeling language (SysML). Initially, adhering to the top-down design principle, we identify stakeholders and core objectives and systematically decompose the mission requirements of the spacecraft. Subsequently, we define the primary functions of the spacecraft, thereby formulating system requirements. Through the integration of these system requirements with the functional definitions, we correlate functional requirements to the system composition and internal structure, culminating in a logical architecture definition for the spacecraft system. Second, by employing SysML behavioral diagrams, we execute flight plan modeling and dynamic logic simulations for the Earth-to-Moon transfer phase of the spacecraft, offering real-time visualizations of the composite state and intersystem signal transmission of the spacecraft. Furthermore, the MagicDraw software is utilized to interface with MATLAB for orbit design performance simulations. This step serves to validate the rationality of the overarching parameters, including incremental orbital velocity and fuel consumption, thus enabling rapid plan iteration. Simultaneously, leveraging design data from source subsystem internal block diagrams, we conducted automatic fault-impact analysis, facilitating efficient calculations and analyses of key attributes such as the minimum cut set. The proposed method is model-centric, ensuring data homology, requirement linkage, unified design verification, and model reuse throughout the design process. This enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of the design scheme, rendering it apt for application in the development of complex spacecraft systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Elevator System Maintenance Strategy Based on Semi-Markov Process
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: A semi-Markov process (SMP)-based maintenance strategy optimization model was built to develop and optimize the preventive maintenance strategy of the elevator system. The model first analyzed the transition relationship of each state of the elevator system and constructed the SMP kernel matrix. The optimal maintenance cycle and steady-state availability of the elevator system were determined. Then, whether the elevator system needs to be repaired or optimized is determined based on the steady-state availability of the system. Three modes of maintenance, which include minor repair, major repair, and replacement, were adopted. Further, the maintenance and cost matrices are introduced to establish a multiobjective optimization model for elevator system maintenance. Finally, a case study demonstrates that the optimization model of maintenance strategy based on SMP can determine the optimal maintenance strategy. The results indicate that compared with the original maintenance strategy, the optimized maintenance strategy can increase the steady-state availability to 0.9999 and the maintenance effect is increased by 27.19%.

articleTitle: Accelerated Storage Life Evaluation Method for Degraded Products Considering Block Effects and Censored Observations
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Constrained by factors such as human and material resources, the random grouping test used in product reliability assessments encounters challenges such as block effects and censored observations. These challenges compound the difficulty and reduce the precision of evaluations. This study introduces a mixed-effects model designed to capture both fixed and random effects within the group data of a degraded product in an aerospace system. Utilizing the maximum likelihood estimation and the best linear unbiased prediction method, the parameters of the mixed-effects model are estimated and lifespan predictions are conducted. A comparison of the results with a traditional model is provided to demonstrate the enhanced performance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Prediction Method for Parameter Degradation and Health Status of DC-DC Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Many studies have been conducted on the DC-DC power module as a power supply system for electronic equipment, owing to its wide range of applications in engineering equipment and its reliability and longevity. In the case of several of these studies, some of the internal devices were separated for the purpose of experimental analysis. However, the results of this separate study are unsuitable for directly characterizing the degraded state of the module, and the assessment of the health status is also one-sided. In this paper, the transient response of a DC-DC circuit is analyzed, and the corresponding test method is determined. The output voltage and number of damping vibrations are determined as degradation characteristic parameters for characterizing the power module degradation status. A new algorithm based on the support vector machine and autoregressive moving-average is proposed to predict the DC-DC characteristic parameters and remaining useful life (RUL). Furthermore, the parameter prediction error of the algorithm is on the order of 10<sup>−3</sup>• In addition, based on the artificial neural network, the health status of the DC-DC module is identified, and the status assessment is completed. Finally, the raw data is processed and analyzed using MATLAB. The RUL and health status of the DC-DC power module are thus evaluated. Through this study, it is possible to accurately predict the degradation of the DC-DC power module and realize the status monitoring of the system in real time.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Energy Ion Implanter for Particle Radiation Testing of Materials in Space Application
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Ion implanters are widely utilized in particle radiation testing of materials within the context of space applications. Their primary purpose is to validate the reliability of materials exposed to space environment. A novel low-energy ion implanter is presently under development, featuring several distinctive attributes aimed at facilitating the production of an ion beam characterized by high uniformity, a substantial irradiation area, and sustained flux stability. The initial step involves the utilization of multi-circle arc-shaped hot cathodes to emit electrons. Subsequently, a multilayer concentric cylindrical electrode, interspersed with hot cathodes, is introduced within the ionization chamber. This configuration paves the way for the ion extraction electrode to extend into the ionization chamber. Finally, an automated adjustment method for regulating ion flux at the target stage is incorporated into the design. These enhancements collectively contribute to heightened efficiency and improved quality in particle radiation testing for materials.

articleTitle: Equivalent Design of Multi-Profile Lab Accelerated Life Test Considering Profile Sequence Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The accelerated life test (ALT) is essential for improving product design and assessing reliability. The equivalent design approach in ALT has garnered increased research attention because of its ability to formulate appropriate test plans as required. This study presents the concept of equivalent design in ALT and establishes equivalence constraints using asymptotic variances. Additionally, it extends the equivalence between laboratory-based ALTs and outdoor field tests. Additionally, we examined the mathematical properties of reliability models considering the sequence effects in multi-profile modeling, thereby providing guidance for model selection. Utilizing the proposed approach, test designers may efficiently create equivalent laboratory-based multi-profile ALTs based on field tests and actual usage data. Moreover, the approach enables flexible adjustment of the test profile sequences, thereby facilitating test scheduling. In conclusion, the study applies a mechanical product as a case study to demonstrate the methodology of this approach and assess its engineering applicability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of 3D Clearance of Torque Link Joint on Landing Gear Taxiing Shaking
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: After a long period of service, the joints in the landing gear of an aircraft may wear and cause a gradual increase in clearances. This ultimately results in shaking during ground taxiing, which can severely affect the pilots' normal operation and result in structural damage to the aircraft. This paper focuses on the landing gear taxiing shaking problem caused by the increase in the clearance of the joint of the torque link. Considering the motion characteristics of the landing gear, this study identifies the effect mechanism of the 3D clearance in the joint of the torque link on landing gear taxiing shaking. Through mathematical analysis, the effect relationship of the 3D clearance in the joint of the torque link on landing gear taxiing shaking is revealed for the first time. The study proposes a rotation joint model based on the LanKarani-Nikravesh (L-N) contact theory that accounts for 3D clearance. The effects of different clearance sizes and types on landing gear taxiing shaking are analyzed in combination with the landing gear taxiing shaking dynamics model. The proposed effect mechanism and effect relationship are verified by comparing the calculation results with the results obtained using the proposed expression. The conclusions of the study can provide important references for landing gear maintenance and the design of anti-shaking function.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Phased-Mission Systems Using Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As the aircraft/engine integrated system evolves, the aircraft's structural composition becomes increasingly complex, system coupling intensifies, and the array of tasks diversifies. Concurrently, the structural configuration, failure criteria, and causal relationships within the aircraft/engine integrated system undergo changes with shifting mission phases, necessitating phased-mission reliability modeling and analysis. Addressing this, this study introduces a phased-mission reliability analysis method for the aircraft/engine integrated system based on Bayesian networks. Initially, we delve into the integrated system's structural composition and operational principles across multiple mission phases, leading to the construction of a multi-phase fault tree. Subsequently, the correlation between the fault tree and the Bayesian network is explored, facilitating the transformation of the fault tree into a Bayesian network model suited for multi-phase missions. Ultimately, system reliability is deduced through forward inference throughout the span of multi-phase missions. Concurrently, using the Bayesian network's reverse inference mechanism, we identify the system's vulnerabilities across different mission phases. The method outlined herein offers pivotal technical support for the reliability design and analysis of aircraft/engine integrated systems.

articleTitle: Quality Supervision of Large and Complex Aerospace Engineering Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Large and complex aerospace engineering projects exhibit notable characteristics, including a complex system structure, elevated technical intricacy, involvement of numerous entities, and stringent quality standards. However, some newly engaged entities may lack familiarity or the requisite competencies to meet high-quality aerospace criteria, thereby introducing substantial risks. The distinctive traits of large and complex aerospace engineering underscore the critical importance of implementing standardized and rigorous quality supervision as the central determinant of product excellence and mission success. This study examined the effective quality supervision practices employed by prominent foreign aerospace enterprises, scrutinized the challenges and issues inherent in quality supervision for large and complex aerospace engineering ventures, and identified key areas for quality supervision enhancement within China's large and complex aerospace engineering domain. These key areas encompass capability assessment, quality assurance representatives, quality supervision mechanisms, accountability protocols, and the management of quality supervision information.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two-step and One-step Methods in Constant Stress Accelerated Degradation Tests
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Our aim is to predict the failure lifetime of a product under normal operating stress conditions in constant stress accelerated degradation tests by analyzing degradation data obtained at high-stress levels. Two commonly used methods for analyzing degradation data are the one-step and two-step methods. The one-step method involves maximizing the likelihood based on degradation data to estimate model parameters, enabling subsequent inference. On the other hand, the two-step method calculates pseudo-lifetimes for each sample and performs accelerated lifetime testing analysis. Advancements in hardware and software computing have improved the computational efficiency of the one-step method, and its performance is now comparable to that of the widely employed two-step method in the industry. This comparative analysis allows us to evaluate the performance and advantages of the one-step method in handling degradation data. In this study, the linear degradation case was considered specifically, and a simulation of the one-step and two-step methods was conducted under degradation path models in constant stress accelerated degradation testing. We used the relative error in the estimation of the mean time to failure (MTTF) as the basis for comparison. Altogether, the one-step method demonstrates higher accuracy and shorter computation time in assessing the MTTF of the product compared to the two-step method, which assumes pseudo-lifetimes and follows three distinct lifetime distributions. This highlights the superiority of the one-step method in handling degradation data, offering the industry a more reliable approach for analysis.

articleTitle: Safety Risk Analysis of Modern Urban Air Logistics System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper addresses the future demand for air logistics application by analyzing safety risk issues in their operation, focusing on the development scenarios of urban air logistics. To achieve this, we establish a simulation model of a modern urban air logistics system. This model incorporates fundamental elements of air traffic, including dispatch centers, transit stations, and aircraft. Using this model, we examine the functions and collaborative relationships of each component to identify potential risk points within an urban air logistics system. Subsequently, we construct a Bayesian network model tailored to urban air logistics scenarios. We achieve this by modeling the identified safety risk factors of the system, taking into account various scenarios such as operator errors, adverse weather conditions, and aircraft failures. We convert the risk fault tree into a Bayesian network, following the established mapping relationship. The paper also entails risk assessment and sensitivity analysis for the urban air logistics system. These analyses help determine the factors that significantly impact the system's operational risk. This information is invaluable for enhancing the design, operation, and safety risk control of air logistics systems, providing essential support in this domain.

articleTitle: Optimal-Condition-Based Maintenance of Cold Standby System with Multiple Operating Units and Multiple Standby Units
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To ensure continuity and security in production processes, a redundancy structure involving multiple units for use and multiple units for standby (MUMS) is typically used. This paper proposes an offline state maintenance decision model for periodic switching and block replacement within the MUMS cold standby system. The concept of maintenance degree is introduced, and a model is established to represent the relationship among the maintenance effect, cost, and time, under the influence of the maintenance degree. By analyzing the alternate state transition characteristics of operating and standby units in the operation process, a steady probability model of the system state is obtained. Subsequently, a model for average rate costs in a limited scope is constructed to determine the optimal system switching period, preventive maintenance threshold, and maintenance degree. The model is validated using a hot roll system. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively reduce the cost rate and ensure system reliability.

articleTitle: The Approach of Equipment Degradation Processes Considering Self-Recovery Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Recent research in the process of equipment state evolution emphasizes the comprehensive consideration of the event process. However, the process does not consider the self-recovery capability of equipment in detail. In view of this problem, a detailed explanation of the self-recovery characteristics is given. Subsequently, a self-recovery model for equipment is established. Furthermore, the degradation process considering self-recovery is established. Finally, a numerical analysis is carried out to give the degradation process curve with self-recovery characteristics. The result shows that the degradation process can reflect the state evolution process more comprehensively for the equipment with self-recovery capability.

articleTitle: Transformer-based fault diagnosis method for fixed-wing UAV elevator
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To address the issue of low aircraft elevator fault diagnosis efficiency, this paper proposes a Transformer-based deep learning fault diagnosis algorithm aimed at enhancing flight safety and fault resolution efficiency. First, data acquisition and processing is described in detail, encompassing data sources, acquisition methods, pre-processing, and feature extraction steps. Subsequently, a fault diagnosis model is designed and assessed in both the training and testing phases. Experimental validation is conducted using actual flight data from an electric drogue fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The paper analyzes the accuracy of the diagnostic model, the trajectory of loss values during iterations, and a comparative assessment against various algorithms to affirm the model's effectiveness and accuracy. Lastly, the paper summarizes the experimental findings and puts forth potential directions for future improvements.

articleTitle: Contact Fatigue Strength Reliability Assessment of Transmission Gears Considering Assembly Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Gears are extensively utilized in mechanical transmissions, where their reliability directly affects the operating efficiency of the whole mechanical system. Surface contact fatigue failure is the most common fault in transmission gears during their service, and therefore deserves key attention to ensure operational safety. During gear work processes, assembly uncertainty serves as an important influencing factor on power transmission performance, thereby inevitably exerting an impact on the reliability of contact fatigue strength (CFS). However, existing studies have not fully considered the effects of assembly uncertainty on the reliability assessment of CFS for gears. In this study, we focus on the reliability assessment issue of CFS for transmission gears with the consideration of multi-source uncertainties including concerned assembly uncertainty. Initially, multi-source uncertainties are introduced which include material dispersion, load randomness and assembly uncertainty, and the assembly parameters of concern are characterized. Thereafter, the performance function for CFS of gears and the corresponding reliability model are adopted, in which Monte Carlo method is employed for the reliability calculation. Then, a pair of spur gears is studied as an example, where stochastic finite element model of the gear pair is established to extract the maximum contact stress. Finally, the case-study results indicate the significant effect of assembly uncertainty on the reliability of gear CFS. Hence, the effect of assembly uncertainty cannot be ignored in gear reliability design.

articleTitle: Research on Mission Chain Scheduling Methods for UAV Swarms Using Intelligent Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) evolve toward swarming and intelligence, the challenges brought about by the complexity and uncertainty of rapidly growing UAV swarms have become more pronounced. These challenges significantly affect the efficiency and reliability of swarm mission execution. Thus, the key to UAV swarm technology is determining effective scheduling techniques that assign tasks to individual UAVs, maximize the global mission benefits, and enhance the reliability of swarm missions. This study delves into the modeling of UAV swarm mission chain scheduling issues and the optimization of mission chain scheduling. Initially, utilizing complex network technology, we represent the mission capability of the mission chain from a flow perspective, constructing a flow network model. Subsequently, by employing two intelligent algorithms—the ant colony algorithm and the genetic algorithm — we build optimization objective functions based on the value trade-off function of the UAV swarm mission chain structure. With mission capability as a constraint, we explore the optimal scheduling strategy for the swarm. We then analyze typical UAV swarm application scenarios as case studies to corroborate the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the proposed methods in engineering practices. Our research lays a foundational framework for decision-making in mission chain scheduling for UAV swarms and analogous systems, ultimately enhancing the reliability of mission execution in related systems.

articleTitle: Sneak Circuit Analysis of Relay Circuits Based on Logic Delay Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Sneak circuit analysis is a vital component of circuit reliability assessment. However, conventional methods for sneak circuit analysis are unsuitable for relay circuits. In this paper, we propose an innovative method for analyzing sneak circuits in relay circuits based on logical delay Petri nets (LDPNs). Based on logic Petri nets, we construct the LDPNs by introducing temporal properties and provide a formal description of relay circuits. Subsequently, rules for abstracting relay circuits as directed graphs and rules for constructing LDPN models are proposed. Employing a railway relay interlocking system as a case study, a relay circuit execution simulation algorithm is proposed based on the evolution principle of LDPNs. This circuit is used to simulate the execution process and final response of the relay circuit under specified excitations. The algorithm facilitates the detection of all pathways during circuit execution, enabling the detection of sneak circuits. Consequently, our proposed methodology can significantly enhance circuit reliability.

articleTitle: Discussion on the Reliability Work of Future Combat Aircraft Under Aircraft/Engine Integrated Design
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Traditional independent methods of aircraft and engine design can no longer meet the mission requirements of future aircraft, including high maneuverability, high energy, large airspace, and wide speed range. To achieve optimal matching between aircraft and engine and promote full play to the maximum performance potential of aircraft and engines, aircraft-engine integration designs are essential. Therefore, considering the highly coupled structure, complex control logic, and dramatic increase in energy and heat dissipation requirements under the integration design to ensure a high mission success rate, corresponding reliability analysis work and reliability level improvement of the whole aircraft are necessary. In this paper, the characteristics of work, structure, environment, and other aspects of aircraft-engine integrated design are initially considered, and the steps to conduct reliability work are discussed.

articleTitle: Safety, Reliability, and Maintainability Assurance Strategy based on Product Risk Level for the Space Station Experimental Payloads
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a safety, reliability, and maintainability (SRM) assurance strategy for space application payloads based on integrated risk measurement. The assurance strategy encompasses product type classification, product risk classification, and distinctive assurance requirements. Building on this foundation and considering the unique attributes of space station payloads for scientific experiments and mission objectives, the paper presents the practical application of SRM assurance. The engineering practice results at the current stage serve as preliminary validation for the suitability and advantages of this assurance scheme for diverse space application payloads. Hence, it offers an efficient solution for subsequent extensive SRM assurance efforts in the field of large-scale space application payloads.

articleTitle: Research Progress on the Cumulative Radiation Effect of InGaAs Infrared Detectors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Shortwave InGaAs infrared detectors are widely used in many commercial and scientific spatial imaging systems. Different types of high-energy particles and radiations are incident on the detector; however, long-term exposure to protons, electrons, and high-energy rays make infrared imaging devices exhibit reliability issues. This article reviews the research on the cumulative radiation effect of InGaAs infrared detectors and provides suggestions for key technologies such as radiation source selection, sensitive parameters, and annealing effects in their radiation reliability evaluation tests.

articleTitle: Universal PHM System Utilizing QFD-MBSE for Unmanned Equipment Design and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: The current approach to designing unmanned equipment fault prediction and health management (PHM) systems relies on testability and expert experience. Unfortunately, this approach often results in a disconnect between the functionality of PHM systems and the actual needs of users, directly impacting the efficiency of unmanned equipment maintenance support. This paper introduces the use of quality function deployment (QFD) theory to analyze the requirements of unmanned equipment PHM systems. It aims to derive system requirements and convert them into system functionality based on stakeholder requirements. To achieve this, a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach is adopted to analyze and design the unmanned equipment PHM system. The QFD-MBSE methodology serves as a guiding framework for the design and development of unmanned equipment PHM systems. It facilitates the process of designing these systems, ensuring alignment from requirements to the final product. This approach enhances the overall design quality of unmanned equipment PHM systems and ensures that the design outcomes align with user requirements.

articleTitle: Exploring Causal Graph Using Graphormer for Complex Systems Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Data-driven fault detection has gained substantial attention in recent times. Graph-based models, which incorporate spatial information for feature extraction, have shown promising results, particularly in the context of increasing system complexity. However, existing models tend to focus solely on adjacent neighbor features, overlooking long-range dependencies. Moreover, many methods assume predefined correlation relationships between variables, potentially limiting their effectiveness. This paper introduces a novel approach: the Causal-Graph-Based Graphormer model for complex system fault detection. It utilizes causal discovery techniques to mine monitoring data, representing causality in graphs. These causal dependencies are then effectively modelled using the Graphormer framework, which encodes both local and long-range features of nodes and edges. To demonstrate its efficacy, a case study involving real high-speed train-braking systems validates the proposed model's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Designing a Flexible Fin Wave Propeller Based on Environmental Adaptability
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Common propellers used to propel traditional underwater robots are susceptible to various environmental factors such as flow rates, aquatic organisms, water quality, and other conditions. These vulnerabilities often lead to system failures or drive mechanism issues. Recognizing the limitations of the conventional underwater propulsion methods in terms of environmental compatibility, this paper introduces a novel approach: the flexible fin wave propulsion drive mode. We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic simulation to validate the feasibility of this propulsion scheme and provide a detailed mechanism design. Thus far, there has been a notable absence of a systematic evaluation method for assessing the environmental adaptability of underwater robots or systems. In response, this paper introduces an environmental adaptability evaluation method based on weighted scoring. This method is applied to evaluate the environmental adaptability of both the traditional propeller-based and the flexible fin wave propulsion methods. The results clearly indicate that the flexible fin wave propulsion drive mode exhibits superior environmental adaptability when compared to traditional propellers.

articleTitle: Reliability Optimization Design Method of Integrated Valve Performance and Potential Failure
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Valves are susceptible to fatigue fractures, long response times, and excessive leakages due to various influencing factors, directly impacting their safety and reliability. This study investigates the random uncertainties associated with performance and potential failure factors in a shifting hydraulic valve. It introduces an integrated analytical approach that combines the Monte Carlo method with uncertainty analysis, addressing both performance and potential failure considerations in reliability optimization design. The results obtained through the proposed method indicate that the reliability of the entire valve can reach 99.92%. This is a significant improvement of 65.49% compared to optimizing solely for performance and a 2.22 % increase compared to focusing solely on potential failure mitigation. The proposed method provides an effective approach for achieving optimal valve reliability design.

articleTitle: Model-Based Forward Design Method for Support System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To address the issue of “two skins” between the model-based support system and military aircraft development within the emerging MBSE development paradigm, this article methodically outlines techniques for the requirement analysis, architectural design, and verification and evaluation of military aircraft support systems rooted in modeling. These techniques follow a “requirements-design-verification” trajectory. Specifically, the paper introduces a modeling method for aviation equipment support capability, employing the Department of Defense Architecture Framework (DODAF) technology to facilitate forward generation of requirements. Additionally, the article advocates a theoretical approach for forward design of the support system architecture, utilizing an axiomatic design process framework in conjunction with model-based system design methods. Targeting both quantitative and qualitative requirements of the support system, verification and evaluation methods are delineated, leveraging a simulation model of support effectiveness and an evaluation criterion model. The article concludes with a case study that substantiates the efficacy of the aforementioned techniques. This study thus offers both theoretical and methodological foundations for the scientifically informed forward design of aviation equipment support systems under the new development paradigm.

articleTitle: Process Quality Control Method for Spacecraft Digital System Design Using Model-Based Systems Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: According to the principle of quality management, we improve the digital expression of the quality management system based on the spacecraft product development process; analyze the development rules of the digital model from three viewpoints of “data attribute, software attribute and product attribute”; formulate the management requirements of digital model review, review, condition control, acceptance, and zero adapted to the model-based systems engineering (MBSE) mode, and acquire practice in the digital development of manned lunar landing engineering aircraft. Improvement directions and suggestions for the quality management body under the digital development mode are further put forward.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearing Based on Multidimensional Feature Extraction and Optimized LSSVM Algorithm
