publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Herein, a multidimensional feature extraction method based on permutation entropy, wavelet packet decomposition, and empirical mode decomposition (EMD); and a stepwise fault diagnosis method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO), artificial bee colony algorithm (ABC) and least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) are proposed for rolling bearings with multiple fault states. First, the normalized bearing initial signal is decomposed by wavelet packet decomposition and EMD. Next, 31-dimensional feature vectors are extracted as input for fault diagnosis classifier. Finally, a three-step fault diagnosis is constructed on the basis of optimized LSSVM classifiers, consisting of fault existence detection, fault localization, and fault degree judgment. According to different steps, the corresponding feature vectors are used as input for the classifiers. Through the simulation analysis of bearing data, the five-fold cross-validation accuracy of the three-step fault diagnosis LSSVM classifier are 100%, (96.3%, 95.2%, 90.9%), and (97.5%, 92.5%, 91.7%). The identification and diagnosis of the fault location and degree of the rolling bearing is realized. Additionally, the validity of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling and Evaluation of an Electric Multiple Unit Incorporating the Mixture Distribution and EM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: As large, complex, highly reliable technical equipment, electric multiple units (EMUs) require long-term maintenance to ensure safety and reliability during service. Because the maintenance cost of an EMU accounts for a large proportion of its entire life-cycle cost, scientific planning of the maintenance interval is vital to reduce maintenance cost and improve maintenance efficiency. This paper proposes a reliability modeling and evaluation approach for EMUs under multi-level maintenance scheduling, with the purpose of extending maintenance intervals and saving maintenance resources. A comprehensive reliability model is established via the mixture distribution approach; accordingly, the point estimation of the mixture distribution model is realized using the EM algorithm. The model feasibility and rationality are highlighted through an engineering case study with actual EMU failure/operational data, where the rationality of extending the maintenance interval (for Level 3 maintenance level) is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnostic Opportunities for Robot Servo Motors Using the Physics of Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: Joint robots are widely used in various industries, such as aviation, aerospace, and automotive manufacturing. The performance degradation of servo motors can significantly affect the overall performance of the robots because of the core component of joint robots, and therefore, it is critical to detect and address servo motor failures promptly. In this study, we analyze some common causes and mechanisms of performance degradation in robot servo motors using the physics of failure analysis. We also discuss strategies for detecting and diagnosing faults using these mechanisms before the servo motors fail completely.

articleTitle: Research on Flight Vibration Environmental Adaptability of Orbit-Control Engine for YZ-3 Upper Stage
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Reliability, Maintainability and Safety (ICRMS)
abstract: To analyze and verify the adaptability of the flight vibration environment of the 5000N orbit-control engine for the YZ-3 upper stage, a simulation analysis and test verification study were carried out for the structural design scheme of the 5000N orbit-control engine. To meet the elasticity and continuity requirements of the finite element simulation analysis method, a finite element model of 5000N orbit-control engine was established under certain assumptions. The finite element model includes a fixed bracket, swing frame, thrust chamber, composite nozzle, servo motor, propellant control valve, shaft sleeve assembly, pipe line components, and heat shield. A structural dynamics simulation analysis of 5000N orbit-control engine was performed. In the first vibration test of the 5000N orbit-control engine, the support ear of the shaft sleeve assembly suffered fatigue fracture. The structural dynamics simulation results were corrected using the actual response data of the vibration test. The maximum stress of the support ear of the shaft sleeve assembly in the x-directional sinusoidal qualification level vibration test was confirmed to exceed the material fatigue limit. Through local structural strengthening and optimization design, the sealing and fixing functions of the cover plate with support ears in the original shaft sleeve assembly were realized, respectively. The 5000N orbit-control engine for YZ-3 upper stage met the adaptability requirements of the flight vibration environment, and the first flight application was successfully completed on December 29, 2018.
